sentences.zh: 周洪謨楊守陳

translations.literal: Zhou Hongmo, Yang Shouchen
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongmo; Yang Shouchen

sentences.zh: （弟守阯子茂元茂仁）〉

translations.literal: (His younger brother was Shouzhi; his sons were Mao, Yuan, and Mao Ren.)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (His younger brother was Shouzhi; his sons were Mao, Yuan, and Mao Ren.)]〉

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanzhen
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanzhen

sentences.zh: （陳音）〉

translations.literal: (Chen Yin)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Chen Yin)]〉

sentences.zh: 傅瀚張昇吳寬傅珪劉春吳儼顧清劉瑞

translations.literal: Fu Han, Zhang Sheng, Wu Kuan, Fu Gui, Liu Chun, Wu Yan, Gu Qing, Liu Rui
translations.idiomatic: Fu Han, Zhang Sheng, Wu Kuan, Fu Gui, Liu Chun, Wu Yan, Gu Qing, and Liu Rui

sentences.zh: 周洪謨，字堯弼，長寧人。

translations.literal: Zhou Hongmo, style name Yaobi, was a native of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongmo, whose style name was Yaobi, came from Changning.

sentences.zh: 正統十年，進士及第。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of the Zhengtong reign, he passed the palace examination as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Zhengtong era (1445), he passed the palace examination as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 授編修。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a compiler at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 博聞強記，善文詞，熟國朝典故，喜談經濟。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with a powerful memory, skilled in literary composition, well versed in the institutions of the dynasty, and fond of discussing statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read with an exceptional memory, excelled at literary composition, knew the institutions of the dynasty thoroughly, and loved to discourse on statecraft.

sentences.zh: 成化改元，廷議討四川山都掌蠻，洪謨上方略六事，詔付軍帥行之。

translations.literal: When the Chenghua reign title was instituted, the court debated campaigning against the Shanduzhang barbarians of Sichuan; Hongmo presented a strategy in six points, and an imperial edict ordered the commanders to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: At the inauguration of the Chenghua reign (1465), as the court debated a campaign against the Shanduzhang tribes of Sichuan, Hongmo submitted a six-point strategy, which the throne ordered the field commanders to implement.

sentences.zh: 進學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 尋為南京祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he became Chancellor of the National University at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 上言南監有紅板倉二十間，高皇后積粟以養監生妻孥者，宜修復。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Southern Directorate had twenty red-board granary rooms in which Empress Gao had stored grain to support the wives and children of students, and that these should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the Nanjing directorate still had twenty red-board granaries where Empress Gao had once stored grain to support students' families, and urged that they be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝允行之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal and had it carried out.

sentences.zh: 母喪服闋，改北監。

translations.literal: After his period of mourning for his mother ended, he was transferred to the Northern Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his mother was over, he was transferred to the Beijing Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，言士風澆浮，請復洪武中學規。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he said that scholarly morals had become shallow and dissolute and requested a restoration of the Academy regulations from the Hongwu period.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chenghua (1475), he reported that student morals had grown lax and asked that the Hongwu-era academy regulations be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納，命禮部榜諭。

translations.literal: The emperor commended and accepted it, ordering the Ministry of Rites to post proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and adopted the proposal, ordering the Ministry of Rites to post notices to the schools.

sentences.zh: 崇信伯費淮入監習禮，久不至。

translations.literal: Believing Baron Fei Huai entered the Directorate to study ritual but long failed to appear.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Baron Fei Huai had been enrolled at the directorate to study ritual but had long stayed away.

sentences.zh: 洪謨劾之，奪冠帶，以儒巾赴監，停歲祿之半，學政肅然。

translations.literal: Hongmo impeached him; his official cap and belt were stripped, he was made to attend the Directorate in a scholar's cap, and half his annual stipend was suspended—the academic administration became strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmo impeached him. His rank insignia was taken away, he was required to attend the academy in a plain scholar's cap, and half his annual stipend was withheld. Discipline at the schools became notably strict.

sentences.zh: 先聖像用冕旒十二，而舞佾豆籩數不稱，洪謨請備天子制。

translations.literal: The image of the Sage Ancestor used twelve tassels on the coronet, but the numbers of dancers, ritual vessels, and libation stands did not match; Hongmo requested that the full imperial rites be provided.
translations.idiomatic: The image of the Sage Ancestor bore a twelve-tasseled coronet, yet the numbers of dancers, libation vessels, and offering stands did not match; Hongmo asked that the full imperial ritual paraphernalia be supplied.

sentences.zh: 又言：「古者鳴球琴瑟為堂上之樂，笙鏞敔為堂下之樂，而干羽則舞於兩階。

translations.literal: He also said: "In antiquity, sounding stones, zithers, and lutes served as music in the hall; flutes, bells, and clappers served as music below the hall; while shields and plumes were danced on the two flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In antiquity, sounding stones, zithers, and lutes were the music of the upper hall; flutes, bells, and clappers were the music of the lower hall; shields and plumes were danced on the two flights of steps.

sentences.zh: 今舞羽居上，樂器居下，非古制，當改。

translations.literal: Today the dance plumes are placed above and the musical instruments below—this is not the ancient system and should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the dance plumes are placed above and the instruments below. This is not the ancient arrangement and should be corrected.

sentences.zh: 」尚書鄒幹駁止之，洪謨再疏爭。

translations.literal: " Minister Zou Gan refuted and halted it; Hongmo memorialized again in protest.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister Zou Gan objected and blocked the change, but Hongmo memorialized again in protest.

sentences.zh: 帝竟俞其議。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of rites on the right.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉左。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was moved to the senior left post.

sentences.zh: 以蔡《傳》所釋璇璣玉衡，後人遵用其制，考驗多不合，宜改制，帝即屬洪謨。

translations.literal: Because the armillary sphere and jade scepter-scale explained in Cai Shen's commentary on the Documents had been followed in later generations but when tested often did not match, they should be redesigned; the emperor immediately assigned this to Hongmo.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary sphere and celestial globe as explained in Cai Shen's commentary on the Documents had been copied by later generations, yet repeated testing showed many discrepancies. Hongmo was told to redesign them, and the emperor put him in charge at once.

sentences.zh: 洪謨易以木，旬日而就。

translations.literal: Hongmo replaced them with wood, and in ten days they were finished.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmo rebuilt them in wood, and they were finished within ten days.

sentences.zh: 十七年進尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Chenghua (1481) he was promoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 二十年加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1484) he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，星變，有所條奏，帝多采納。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when stars changed abnormally, he submitted various memorials, and the emperor adopted many of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1485), after an irregularity in the heavens, he submitted a series of memorials, most of which the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年四月，天壽山震雷風雹，樓殿瓦獸多毀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Hongzhi, at Tianshou Mountain there were earthquakes, thunder, wind, and hail; many roof tiles and ornamental beasts on the halls were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Hongzhi (1488), Tianshou Mountain was struck by earthquake, thunder, wind, and hail, and many roof tiles and ridge ornaments on the halls were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 洪謨復力勸修省，帝深納之。

translations.literal: Hongmo again strongly urged self-examination and reform; the emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmo again urged the emperor to examine himself and reform his conduct, and the emperor took the advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 洪謨矜莊寡合，與萬安同鄉，安居政府時頗與之善。

translations.literal: Hongmo was dignified and aloof, rarely associating with others; he was a fellow townsman of Wan An, and when An held power in the government they were on fairly good terms.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmo was dignified and reserved, keeping few close associates. He was from the same district as Wan An, and while An dominated the government they had been on friendly terms.

sentences.zh: 至是，言官先後論奏，致仕歸。

translations.literal: At this time censors memorialized against him in succession, and he retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: By then censors had memorialized against him one after another, and he retired to his home.

sentences.zh: 又三年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: Three years later he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 謚文安。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wen'an (Cultured and Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 洪謨嘗言：「士人出仕，或去鄉數千里，既昧土俗，亦拂人情，不若就近選除。

translations.literal: Hongmo once said: "When scholars take office, some go thousands of li from their home districts; they are ignorant of local customs and run counter to human feelings—it would be better to appoint them nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmo once said: "When scholars take office, some are posted thousands of li from home. They neither know local customs nor can respond to local needs. It would be better to appoint them near their own districts.

sentences.zh: 王府官終身不遷，乖祖制，當稍變更。

translations.literal: Officials of princely establishments never transfer throughout their lives, which departs from the ancestral institutions and should be somewhat changed.
translations.idiomatic: Princely household officials never transfer for life, which departs from the ancestral system and ought to be revised.

sentences.zh: 都掌蠻及白羅羅羿子數叛，宜特設長官司，就擇其人任之，庶無後患。

translations.literal: The Shanduzhang barbarians and the White Luoluo and Yizi have rebelled repeatedly; special native-official posts should be established and suitable men chosen to fill them, so that there may be no trouble afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanduzhang tribes and the White Luoluo and Yizi have rebelled repeatedly. Special native-official posts should be created and capable men chosen from among them to fill them, so as to forestall further trouble.

sentences.zh: 」將歿，猶上安中國、定四裔十事。

translations.literal: " As he was about to die, he still submitted ten items on securing China and settling the four borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: " On his deathbed he still submitted ten proposals on securing the heartland and stabilizing the border peoples.

sentences.zh: 其好建白如此。

translations.literal: Such was his fondness for offering proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his habit of offering forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 楊守陳，字維新，鄞人。

translations.literal: Yang Shouchen, style name Weixin, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouchen, whose style name was Weixin, came from Yin (Ningbo).

sentences.zh: 祖範，有學行，嘗誨守陳以精思實踐之學。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fan was a man of learning and conduct and once instructed Shouchen in the learning of careful thought and earnest practice.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fan was a scholar of moral weight who had taught Shouchen to pursue learning through careful thought and earnest practice.

sentences.zh: 舉景泰二年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jingtai reign, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jingtai (1451), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 成化初，充經筵講官，進侍講。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium and was promoted to court lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium and was promoted to court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 《英宗實錄》成，遷洗馬。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong were completed, he was transferred to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong were completed, he was made a reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 尋進侍講學士，同修《宋元通鑒綱目》。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to lecturer-academician and helped compile the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror from Song and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to lecturer-academician and helped compile the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror from Song and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 母憂服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: When his mourning for his mother ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his mother was over, he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 孝宗出閣，為東宮講官。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor left the inner quarters, he became a lecturer in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Xiaozong Emperor left the inner quarters, Shouchen became a lecturer in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 時編《文華大訓》，事涉宦官者皆不錄。

translations.literal: At that time they were compiling the Great Instructions of Wenhua, and matters involving eunuchs were all omitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was compiling the Great Instructions of Wenhua, and anything involving eunuchs was left out.

sentences.zh: 守陳以為非，備列其善惡得失。

translations.literal: Shouchen considered this wrong and set forth in full their good and bad deeds and their gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Shouchen thought this wrong and set out in full their good and bad deeds and what had been gained or lost.

sentences.zh: 書成，進少詹事。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was promoted to junior mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he was promoted to junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，宮僚悉遷秩，執政擬守陳南京吏部右侍郎，帝舉筆去「南京」字。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded to the throne, all Eastern Palace officials were promoted in rank; the chief ministers proposed Shouchen as Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing, and the emperor raised his brush and deleted the word "Nanjing."
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded to the throne, all former Eastern Palace officials were promoted. The chief ministers proposed Shouchen for vice minister of personnel at Nanjing, but the emperor struck out the word "Nanjing."

sentences.zh: 左右言劉宣見為右侍郎，帝乃改宣左，而以守陳代之。

translations.literal: Those beside him said that Liu Xuan was already vice minister on the right, so the emperor moved Xuan to the left and had Shouchen replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants pointed out that Liu Xuan already held the right vice ministership, so the emperor moved Xuan to the left post and gave the right post to Shouchen.

sentences.zh: 修《憲宗實錄》，充副總裁。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were compiled, he served as associate chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: While compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, he served as associate chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元正月，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the first month when the Hongzhi reign title was instituted, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the Hongzhi reign (1488), he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 孟子言「我非堯舜之道不敢陳於王前。

translations.literal: Mencius said, "Unless it is the way of Yao and Shun, I dare not set it forth before the king.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, "Unless it is the way of Yao and Shun, I dare not set it forth before the king.

sentences.zh: 」夫堯舜之道何道？

translations.literal: " What way is the way of Yao and Shun?
translations.idiomatic: " What, then, is the way of Yao and Shun?

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中」，此堯、舜之得於內者深，而為出治之本也。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discriminating and unified; hold fast the mean in sincerity." This shows how deeply Yao and Shun attained within themselves, and it is the root of bringing order forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discriminating and unified; hold fast the mean in sincerity." This is how deeply Yao and Shun cultivated themselves within, and it is the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 詢四嶽，辟四門，明四目，達四聰，此堯、舜之資於外者博，而為致治之綱也。

translations.literal: "Consult the Four Peaks, open the four gates, sharpen the four eyes, and extend the four ears"—this shows how broadly Yao and Shun drew upon what lay outside themselves, and it is the framework for achieving order.
translations.idiomatic: "Consult the Four Peaks, open the four gates, sharpen the four eyes, and extend the four ears"—this is how broadly Yao and Shun drew on the world beyond themselves, and it is the framework for bringing order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣昔忝宮僚，伏睹陛下朗讀經書，未嘗勤睿問以究聖賢奧旨。

translations.literal: Your servant once had the honor of serving in the Eastern Palace and observed Your Majesty reading the classics aloud, yet never with diligent penetrating questions to plumb the profound meaning of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once had the honor of serving in the Eastern Palace and observed Your Majesty reading the classics aloud, yet never pressing keen questions to reach the sages' deepest meaning.

sentences.zh: 儒臣略陳訓詁，未嘗進詳說以極帝王要道。

translations.literal: Confucian officials briefly explained glosses but never offered detailed exposition to reach the essential way of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian lecturers offered only brief glosses and never gave full exposition of what emperors and kings must know.

sentences.zh: 是陛下得於內者未深也。

translations.literal: Thus what Your Majesty has attained within is not yet deep.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that what Your Majesty has attained within is not yet deep enough.

sentences.zh: 今視朝，所接見者，大臣之豐采而已。

translations.literal: Now at court audiences, those whom you meet are only the bearing and appearance of high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At court audiences today, those whom you meet are only the bearing and appearance of senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 君子、小人之情狀，小臣、遠臣之才行，何由識？

translations.literal: How can you know the conduct of gentlemen and petty men, or the ability and conduct of junior and distant officials?
translations.idiomatic: How can you know the conduct of the worthy and the unworthy, or the talent and character of junior and distant officials?

sentences.zh: 退朝所披閱者，百官之章奏而已。

translations.literal: After court, what you peruse is only the memorials of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: After court, what you read is only the memorials of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 諸司之典則，群吏之情弊，何由見？

translations.literal: How can you see the regulations of the various offices or the abuses among the clerks?
translations.idiomatic: How can you see the regulations of the various offices or the abuses among the clerks?

sentences.zh: 宮中所聽信者，內臣之語言而已。

translations.literal: Within the palace, what you hear and trust is only the words of inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, what you hear and trust is only the words of eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 百官之正議，萬姓之繁言，何由聞？

translations.literal: How can you hear the upright opinions of the hundred officials or the many voices of the myriad people?
translations.idiomatic: How can you hear the upright opinions of officials or the many voices of the people?

sentences.zh: 恐陛下資於外者未博也。

translations.literal: I fear that what Your Majesty draws upon from without is not yet broad.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that what Your Majesty draws upon from without is not yet broad enough.

sentences.zh: 願遵祖宗舊制，開大小經筵，日再禦朝。

translations.literal: I wish that Your Majesty would follow the ancestral institutions, open both the great and small Classics Colloquia, and hold court twice daily.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty follow the ancestral institutions, restore both the great and small Classics Colloquia, and hold court twice each day.

sentences.zh: 大經筵及早朝，但如舊儀。

translations.literal: The great Classics Colloquium and the early audience should follow the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: The great Classics Colloquium and the early audience should follow the established rites.

sentences.zh: 若小經筵，必擇端方博雅之臣，更番進講。

translations.literal: As for the small Classics Colloquium, upright and broadly learned officials must be chosen to lecture in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: For the small Classics Colloquium, upright and broadly learned officials should be chosen to lecture in rotation.

sentences.zh: 凡所未明，輒賜清問。

translations.literal: Whenever anything is unclear, grant clarifying questions at once.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anything is unclear, Your Majesty should press for explanation.

sentences.zh: 凡聖賢經旨，帝王大道，以及人臣賢否，政事得失，民情休戚，必講之明而無疑，乃可行之篤而無弊。

translations.literal: Whatever concerns the meaning of the sages' classics, the great way of emperors and kings, the worthiness or unworthiness of ministers, the gains and losses of government affairs, or the weal and woe of the people must be explained until it is clear and beyond doubt; only then may it be carried out steadfastly and without harm.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever concerns the meaning of the classics, the way of kingship, the worthiness of ministers, the success or failure of policy, or the welfare of the people must be discussed until it is clear beyond doubt; only then can it be carried out steadfastly and without harm.

sentences.zh: 若夫前朝經籍，祖宗典訓，百官章奏，皆當貯文華殿後，陛下退朝披覽。

translations.literal: As for the classics of former dynasties, the ancestral instructions, and the memorials of the hundred officials, all should be stored behind the Wenhua Hall, and after court Your Majesty should peruse them.
translations.idiomatic: The classics of former dynasties, the ancestral instructions, and officials' memorials should all be kept behind Wenhua Hall for Your Majesty to read after court.

sentences.zh: 日令內閣一人、講官二人居前殿右廂，有疑則詢，必洞晰而後已。

translations.literal: Each day one member of the Grand Secretariat and two lecturers should sit in the right wing of the front hall; when there are doubts, inquire of them, and do not stop until everything is thoroughly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Each day one grand secretary and two lecturers should sit in the right wing of the front hall. When doubts arise, ask them, and do not stop until everything is thoroughly clear.

sentences.zh: 一日之間，居文華殿之時多，處乾清宮之時少，則欲寡心清，臨政不惑，得於內者深而出治之本立矣。

translations.literal: If within a single day you spend more time in the Wenhua Hall and less in the Qianqing Palace, then desires will be few, the mind clear, and in governing you will not be confused—what is attained within will be deep and the root of bringing order forth will be established.
translations.idiomatic: If within a single day you spend more time in Wenhua Hall and less in the Qianqing Palace, desires will be few and the mind clear; in governing you will not be confused. What is attained within will be deep, and the foundation of good government will be laid.

sentences.zh: 午朝則禦文華門，大臣臺諫更番侍直。

translations.literal: At the noon audience, hold court at the Wenhua Gate, with high ministers and censors of the surveillance and remonstrance bureaus attending in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: At the noon audience, hold court at Wenhua Gate, with senior ministers and censorial officials attending in rotation.

sentences.zh: 事已具疏者用揭帖，略節口奏，陛下詳問而裁決之。

translations.literal: For matters already set forth in memorials, use summary slips, abridge them in oral report, and let Your Majesty question closely and decide.
translations.idiomatic: For matters already submitted in full memorials, use summary slips and brief oral reports; Your Majesty should question closely and decide.

sentences.zh: 在外文武官來覲，俾條列地方事，口陳大要，付諸司評議。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials from outside come to audience, have them list local affairs item by item, state the main points orally, and refer them to the relevant offices for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When officials from the provinces come to audience, have them list local affairs item by item, state the main points orally, and refer the matters to the relevant offices for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 其陛辭赴任者，隨其職任而戒諭之。

translations.literal: Those taking leave of the throne to proceed to their posts should be admonished according to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Those taking leave of the throne to proceed to their posts should be admonished according to their duties.

sentences.zh: 有大政則禦文華殿，使大臣各盡其謀，勿相推避。

translations.literal: When there is great policy, hold court in the Wenhua Hall and have the high ministers each offer their counsel fully, without shirking or passing responsibility to one another.
translations.idiomatic: When major policy is at issue, hold court in Wenhua Hall and have senior ministers each offer their counsel fully, without shirking or passing responsibility to one another.

sentences.zh: 不當則許言官駁正。

translations.literal: If it is improper, allow censors to refute and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: If a proposal is improper, allow censors to refute and correct it.

sentences.zh: 其他具疏進者，召閣臣面議可否，然後批答。

translations.literal: For other matters submitted in memorials, summon the Grand Secretariat members to discuss face to face whether they are feasible, and only then draft the rescript.
translations.idiomatic: For other matters submitted in memorials, summon grand secretaries to discuss them face to face, and only then draft the rescript.

sentences.zh: 而於奏事、辭朝諸臣，必降詞色，詳詢博訪，務竭下情，使賢才常接於目前，視聽不偏於左右，合天下之耳目以為聰明，則資於外者博而致治之綱舉矣。

translations.literal: Toward those who memorialize on affairs or take leave of court, you must lower your tone and show kindness, inquire closely and seek broadly, and strive to exhaust the sentiments below, so that worthy talent is constantly before your eyes, sight and hearing are not biased to those at your side, and the ears and eyes of all under Heaven are joined as your intelligence—then what is drawn upon from without will be broad and the framework for achieving order will be raised up.
translations.idiomatic: Toward those who memorialize or take leave of court, speak gently and inquire closely, striving to hear all that lies below. Let worthy talent always stand before you; let sight and hearing not be confined to those at your side. Unite the ears and eyes of the realm as your own intelligence—then what is drawn upon from without will be broad, and the framework for good government will be in place.

sentences.zh: 若如經筵、常朝只循故事，凡百章奏皆付內臣調旨批答，臣恐積弊未革，後患滋深。

translations.literal: If the Classics Colloquium and regular audiences merely follow precedent, and all memorials are handed to inner attendants to draft rescripts and reply, your servant fears that accumulated abuses will not be reformed and later troubles will grow deeper.
translations.idiomatic: If the Classics Colloquium and regular audiences merely follow precedent, and all memorials are handed to eunuchs to draft rescripts, I fear accumulated abuses will remain and later troubles will only deepen.

sentences.zh: 且今積弊不可勝數。

translations.literal: Moreover, accumulated abuses today are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the abuses that have accumulated today are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 官鮮廉恥之風，士多浮競之習。

translations.literal: Among officials, the spirit of integrity and shame is rare; among scholars, habits of empty rivalry are many.
translations.idiomatic: Among officials, integrity and shame are rare; among scholars, empty rivalry is common.

sentences.zh: 教化淩夷，刑禁馳懈。

translations.literal: Education and transformation have declined, and penal prohibitions have grown lax.
translations.idiomatic: Moral instruction has declined, and penal enforcement has grown lax.

sentences.zh: 俗侈而財滋乏，民困而盜日繁。

translations.literal: Customs are extravagant while resources grow scarce; the people are distressed while banditry daily increases.
translations.idiomatic: Luxury spreads while resources grow scarce; the people are distressed and banditry increases daily.

sentences.zh: 列衛之城池不修，諸郡之倉庫鮮積。

translations.literal: The city walls of the guard units are not repaired, and the granaries of the various prefectures have little stored.
translations.idiomatic: The walls of the guard garrisons are not repaired, and prefectural granaries hold little grain.

sentences.zh: 甲兵朽鈍，行伍空虛。

translations.literal: Armor and weapons are rotten and blunt; the ranks are empty.
translations.idiomatic: Armor and weapons are rotten and blunt; the ranks stand empty.

sentences.zh: 將驕惰而不知兵，士疲弱而不習戰。

translations.literal: Generals are arrogant and indolent and do not understand warfare; soldiers are weak and weary and do not practice fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Generals are arrogant and indolent and do not understand warfare; soldiers are weak and untrained for battle.

sentences.zh: 一或有警，何以禦之？

translations.literal: If there should be an alarm, how could it be met?
translations.idiomatic: If an emergency arises, how can the realm be defended?

sentences.zh: 此臣所以朝夕憂思，至或廢寢忘食者也。

translations.literal: This is why your servant worries morning and evening, sometimes even neglecting sleep and forgetting to eat.
translations.idiomatic: This is why I worry morning and evening, sometimes even neglecting sleep and forgetting to eat.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial deeply and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 後果復午朝，召大臣面議政事，皆自守陳發之。

translations.literal: Afterward the noon audience was indeed restored, and high ministers were summoned to discuss government face to face—all of this originated with Shouchen.
translations.idiomatic: The noon audience was indeed restored afterward, and senior ministers were summoned to discuss policy face to face—all of this began with Shouchen's memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋以史事繁，乞解部務。

translations.literal: Soon, because historical work was burdensome, he requested to be relieved of his ministry duties.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing the press of historical compilation, he asked to be relieved of his ministry duties.

sentences.zh: 章三上，乃以本官兼詹事府，專事史館。

translations.literal: After three memorials, he was given his original rank while also serving in the Household of the Heir Apparent, devoting himself solely to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting three memorials, he was allowed to keep his rank while also serving in the Household of the Heir Apparent, devoting himself solely to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Hongzhi (1489) he died.

sentences.zh: 謚文懿，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wenyi, and he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenyi (Cultured and Virtuous) and was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 弟守阯。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Shouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Shouzhi.

sentences.zh: 子茂元、茂仁。

translations.literal: His sons were Maoyuan and Maoren.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Maoyuan and Maoren.

sentences.zh: 守阯，字維立。

translations.literal: Shouzhi, style name Weili.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi, whose style name was Weili.

sentences.zh: 成化初，鄉試第一，入國學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua he ranked first in the provincial examination and entered the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chenghua he ranked first in the provincial examination and entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 祭酒邢讓下獄，率六館生伏闕訟冤。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Xing Rang was imprisoned, he led students of the six halls to kneel before the palace gate and plead his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Xing Rang was imprisoned, he led students of the six halls to kneel before the palace gate and plead his innocence.

sentences.zh: 十四年，進士及第。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he passed the palace examination as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua (1478) he passed the palace examination as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 授編修。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a compiler at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，故事無遷留都者。

translations.literal: When his term ended, precedent held that none who remained in the capital were transferred.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, precedent held that compilers who remained in the capital were not transferred.

sentences.zh: 會從兄守隨為李孜省所逐，欲並逐守阯，乃以為南京侍讀。

translations.literal: It happened that his cousin Shousui had been driven out by Li Zisheng, who wished to drive out Shouzhi as well; he was therefore made reader at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Shousui had been driven from office by Li Zisheng, who wished to drive out Shouzhi as well; Shouzhi was therefore posted as reader at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，召修《憲宗實錄》，直經筵，再遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, served at the Classics Colloquium, and was twice promoted to lecturer-academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, served at the Classics Colloquium, and was twice promoted to lecturer-academician.

sentences.zh: 給事中龐泮等以救知州劉遜悉下獄，吏部尚書屠滽奏遣他官攝之。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Pang Pan and others, for having tried to save Prefect Liu Xun, were all imprisoned; Minister of Personnel Tu Yong memorialized to send another official to act in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Pang Pan and others, for having tried to save Prefect Liu Xun, were all imprisoned; Minister of Personnel Tu Yong memorialized to send another official to act in their place.

sentences.zh: 守阯貽書，極詆滽失。

translations.literal: Shouzhi sent a letter fiercely denouncing Yong's error.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi sent a letter fiercely denouncing Yong's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 十年大計京官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year came the great evaluation of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year came the great evaluation of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 守阯時掌院事，言：「臣與掌詹事府學士王鏊，俱當聽部考察。

translations.literal: Shouzhi was then in charge of the Academy and said: "Your servant and Wang Ao, academician in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent, should both submit to evaluation by the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi was then in charge of the Hanlin Academy and said: "Your servant and Wang Ao, academician in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent, should both submit to evaluation by the ministry.

sentences.zh: 但臣等各有屬員。

translations.literal: But your servant and the others each have subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: But each of us has subordinates.

sentences.zh: 進與吏部會考所屬，則坐堂上，退而聽考，又當候階下。

translations.literal: If we go in and join the Ministry of Personnel in evaluating our subordinates, we sit in the hall above, then withdraw to be evaluated ourselves, and must again wait below the steps.
translations.idiomatic: If we join the Ministry of Personnel in evaluating our subordinates, we sit in the hall above; then we withdraw to be evaluated ourselves and must wait below the steps.

sentences.zh: 我朝優假學士，慶成侍宴，班四品上，車駕臨雍，坐彜倫堂內，視三品，此故事也。

translations.literal: Our dynasty treats academicians with special favor: at the celebration of completion they attend banquets ranked above the fourth grade; when the imperial carriage visits the Academy they sit inside the Hall of Human Relations, treated as third grade—this is established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty treats academicians with special favor: at completion banquets they are ranked above the fourth grade; when the emperor visits the Academy they sit inside the Hall of Human Relations, treated as third grade—this is established precedent.

sentences.zh: 今四品不與考察，則學士亦不應與。

translations.literal: If fourth-grade officials are not subject to evaluation, then academicians should not be either.
translations.idiomatic: If fourth-grade officials are not subject to evaluation, then academicians should not be either.

sentences.zh: 臣等職講讀撰述，稱否在聖鑒，有不待考察者。

translations.literal: Your servant and the others lecture, read, and compose; praise or blame lies in the sage mirror, and there are matters that need no evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Our duties are lecturing, reading, and composing; praise or blame lies in the emperor's judgment, and there are matters that need no formal evaluation.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 學士不與考察，自守阯始。

translations.literal: That academicians were not subject to evaluation began with Shouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The exemption of academicians from evaluation began with Shouzhi.

sentences.zh: 修《會典》，充副總裁。

translations.literal: When the Collected Statutes were compiled, he served as associate chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: While compiling the Collected Statutes, he served as associate chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南京吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of personnel at Nanjing on the right.

sentences.zh: 嘗署兵部，陳時弊五事。

translations.literal: He once acted for the Ministry of War and set forth five current abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He once acted for the Ministry of War and set forth five current abuses.

sentences.zh: 改署國子監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to act for the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to act for the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 考績入都，《會典》猶未成，仍留為總裁。

translations.literal: When he came to the capital for performance evaluation, the Collected Statutes were still unfinished, and he was kept on as chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to the capital for performance evaluation, the Collected Statutes were still unfinished, and he was kept on as chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 事竣，遷左侍郎還任，進二秩。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he was transferred to the left vice ministership and returned to his post, advanced two grades in rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he was promoted to the left vice ministership and returned to his post, advanced two grades in rank.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，引年乞休，不待報竟歸，詔加尚書致仕。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor succeeded, citing his years he requested retirement; without waiting for a reply he returned home, and an edict added the title of minister for his retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong Emperor succeeded, citing his years he requested retirement; without waiting for a reply he went home, and an edict granted him the rank of minister on retirement.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾亂政，奪其加官，瑾敗乃復，久之卒。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin threw the government into disorder, his added rank was stripped; after Jin's fall it was restored, and after a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin threw the government into disorder, his added rank was stripped; after Jin's fall it was restored. He died some years later.

sentences.zh: 守阯博極群書，師事兄守陳，學行相埒。

translations.literal: Shouzhi read exhaustively among all books, took his elder brother Shouchen as teacher, and in learning and conduct was his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhi read widely across the classics, studied under his elder brother Shouchen, and matched him in learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 其為解元、學士、侍郎，皆與兄同。

translations.literal: His becoming provincial first, academician, and vice minister were all the same as his brother's.
translations.idiomatic: His posts as provincial first, academician, and vice minister all paralleled his brother's career.

sentences.zh: 又對掌兩京翰林院，人尤艷稱之。

translations.literal: Moreover, they concurrently headed the Hanlin Academies of the two capitals, which people especially admired and praised.
translations.idiomatic: They also concurrently headed the Hanlin Academies of the two capitals, which people especially admired.

sentences.zh: 守陳卒，守阯為位哭奠者三年。

translations.literal: When Shouchen died, Shouzhi set up a mourning place and wept and offered sacrifices for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchen died, Shouzhi maintained a mourning place and wept and offered sacrifices for three years.

sentences.zh: 茂元，字誌仁。

translations.literal: Maoyuan, style name Zhiren.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan, whose style name was Zhiren.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Chenghua (1475).

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中，出為湖廣副使，改山東。

translations.literal: He rose through bureau director and went out as vice commissioner of Huguang, then was transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to bureau director, then was posted as vice commissioner in Huguang and later transferred to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年，河決張秋，詔都御史劉大夏治之，復遣中官李興、平江伯陳銳繼往。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongzhi the Yellow River burst its banks at Zhangqiu; an edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Liu Daxia to repair it, and eunuch Li Xing and the Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Rui, were again sent to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Hongzhi (1494) the Yellow River burst its banks at Zhangqiu. The throne ordered Censor-in-Chief Liu Daxia to repair the breach and also sent the eunuch Li Xing and the Earl of Pingjiang, Chen Rui, to assist.

sentences.zh: 興威虐，縶辱按察使。

translations.literal: Xing was brutal and tyrannical and bound and humiliated the surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was brutal and tyrannical and bound and humiliated the surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 茂元攝司事，奏言：「治河之役，官多而責不專。

translations.literal: Maoyuan was acting commissioner and memorialized: "In the river-control project, officials are many but responsibility is not concentrated.
translations.idiomatic: Maoyuan was acting commissioner and memorialized: "In the river-control project, officials are too many and responsibility is not concentrated.

sentences.zh: 有司供億，日費百金。

translations.literal: The local offices supply provisions, spending a hundred taels of gold each day.
translations.idiomatic: Local offices supply provisions at a cost of a hundred taels of silver each day.

sentences.zh: 諸臣初祭河，天色陰晦，帛不能燃。

translations.literal: When the officials first sacrificed to the river, the sky was dark and overcast and the silk could not burn.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials first sacrificed to the river, the sky was dark and overcast and the silk offerings would not burn.

sentences.zh: 所焚之余，宛然人面，具耳目口鼻，觀者駭異。

translations.literal: Among what was burned, there clearly remained a human face, complete with ears, eyes, mouth, and nose; those who saw it were struck with horror and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Among what was burned, there clearly remained a human face, complete with ears, eyes, mouth, and nose. Those who saw it were struck with horror.

sentences.zh: 鬼神示怪，夫豈偶然？

translations.literal: Spirits and gods showing strangeness—how could this be accidental?
translations.idiomatic: When spirits show such signs, how can it be mere chance?

sentences.zh: 乞召還興、銳等，專委大夏，功必可成。

translations.literal: I beg that Xing, Rui, and the others be recalled and the task entrusted solely to Daxia; the work will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Xing, Rui, and the others be recalled and the task entrusted solely to Daxia; the work will surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 且水者陰象，今後戚家威權太盛，假名姓肆貪暴者，不可勝數，請加禁防，以消變異。

translations.literal: Moreover, water is a yin emblem; today the power of the empress's kin is too great, and those who borrow names to indulge in greed and violence are beyond counting. I ask that prohibitions be strengthened to dispel these anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, water is a yin emblem. Today the power of the empress's kin is too great, and those who borrow their names to indulge in greed and violence are beyond counting. I ask that prohibitions be strengthened to dispel these portents.

sentences.zh: 畫工、藝士，宜悉放遣。

translations.literal: Painters and artisans should all be dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Painters and artisans should all be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 山東既有內臣鎮守，復令李全鎮臨清，宜撤還。

translations.literal: Shandong already has an inner attendant garrisoning it, yet Li Quan was again ordered to garrison Linqing; he should be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong already has an eunuch garrison commander, yet Li Quan was again posted to Linqing; he should be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下山東撫、按勘，奏言：「焚帛之異誠有之，所奏供億，多過其實。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, the Shandong grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner were ordered to investigate; they reported: "The anomaly of the burning silk truly occurred, but the reported provisioning expenses mostly exceed the facts.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the Shandong grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner were ordered to investigate. They reported: "The anomaly of the burning silk truly occurred, but the reported provisioning expenses mostly exceed the facts.

sentences.zh: 」於是興、銳連章劾茂元妄，詔遣錦衣百戶胡節逮之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xing and Rui submitted successive memorials impeaching Maoyuan for recklessness; an edict sent the Embroidered Uniform Guard hundred-household head Hu Jie to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Xing and Rui submitted successive memorials accusing Maoyuan of recklessness, and an edict sent the Embroidered Uniform Guard officer Hu Jie to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 父老遮道訴節，乞還楊副使。

translations.literal: Elders blocked the road and appealed to Jie, begging that Vice Commissioner Yang be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Local elders blocked the road and appealed to Jie, begging that Vice Commissioner Yang be returned.

sentences.zh: 及陛見，茂元長跪不伏，帝怒，置之詔獄。

translations.literal: When he was presented at court, Maoyuan knelt long without submitting; the emperor was angry and placed him in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When he was presented at court, Maoyuan knelt but refused to submit. The emperor was angry and placed him in the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 節遍叩中官，備言父老訴冤狀，中官多感動。

translations.literal: Jie went about among the inner attendants and fully described how the elders had pleaded their grievances; many of the eunuchs were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Jie went among the eunuchs and fully described how the elders had pleaded their grievances; many were moved.

sentences.zh: 會言者交論救，部擬贖杖還職，特謫長沙同知。

translations.literal: As censors memorialized in succession to save him, the ministry proposed redemption by cane and return to office, but he was specially demoted to vice prefect of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: As censors memorialized in succession to save him, the ministry proposed redemption by cane and return to office, but he was specially demoted to vice prefect of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起安慶知府，遷廣西左參政。

translations.literal: After a long time he was recalled as prefect of Anqing and transferred to Left Administrative Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled as prefect of Anqing and promoted to left administrative commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，劉瑾遣御史孫迪校勘錢穀，索賄不予。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde, Liu Jin sent Censor Sun Di to audit revenue and grain accounts; Maoyuan refused to give a bribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengde (1509), Liu Jin sent Censor Sun Di to audit revenue and grain accounts; Maoyuan refused to pay a bribe.

sentences.zh: 瑾又惡茂元從父守隨，遂勒致仕。

translations.literal: Jin also hated Maoyuan's cousin Shousui and therefore forced him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also hated Maoyuan's cousin Shousui and therefore forced Maoyuan to retire.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起官江西，尋遷雲南左布政使。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, he was recalled to office in Jiangxi and soon transferred to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he was recalled to office in Jiangxi and soon made left provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫貴州，改蒞南京都察院，終刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: As Vice Censor-in-Chief on the right he toured and pacified Guizhou, then took charge of the Nanjing Censorate, and ended as Vice Minister of Justice on the right.
translations.idiomatic: As vice censor-in-chief on the right he served as grand coordinator of Guizhou, then took charge of the Nanjing Censorate, and ended his career as vice minister of justice on the right.

sentences.zh: 茂仁，字志道，成化末進士。

translations.literal: Maoren, style name Zhidao, a jinshi at the end of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Maoren, whose style name was Zhidao, passed the jinshi examination late in Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He served as bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served as bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 遼東鎮守中官梁玘被劾，偕給事中往按，盡發其罪。

translations.literal: The Liaodong garrison eunuch Liang Qi was impeached; Maoren went with a supervising secretary to investigate and fully exposed his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong garrison eunuch Liang Qi was impeached; Maoren went with a supervising secretary to investigate and fully exposed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 終四川按察使。

translations.literal: He ended as Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 張元禎，字廷祥，南昌人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanzhen, style name Tingxiang, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanzhen, whose style name was Tingxiang, came from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 五歲能詩，寧靖王召見，命名元征。

translations.literal: At five he could compose poetry; the Prince of Ningjing summoned him and named him Yuanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: At five he could compose poetry; the Prince of Ningjing summoned him and gave him the name Yuanzheng.

sentences.zh: 巡撫韓雍器之曰「人瑞也」，乃易元禎。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Han Yong admired him and said, "A human auspice," and therefore changed his name to Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Han Yong admired him and said, "A human auspice," and therefore changed his name to Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 舉天順四年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Tianshun, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Tianshun (1460), entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗣位，疏請行三年喪，不省。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he memorialized requesting that the three-year mourning be observed; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he memorialized requesting that the three-year mourning be observed; the court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，疏陳三事：「一，勤講學。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he memorialized setting forth three matters: "First, diligently pursue the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year he memorialized setting forth three matters: "First, diligently pursue the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 願不廢寒暑，所講必切於修德為治之實，不必以亂亡忌觸為諱。

translations.literal: I wish that it not be suspended in cold or heat; what is lectured must bear on the substance of cultivating virtue and governing, and need not avoid taboo topics of disorder and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that lectures not be suspended in cold or heat; what is taught must bear on cultivating virtue and governing, and need not avoid taboo topics of disorder and ruin.

sentences.zh: 講退，更凝神靜味，驗之於身心政化。

translations.literal: After lectures, concentrate the spirit and quietly savor them, testing them in body, mind, and political transformation.
translations.idiomatic: After lectures, concentrate the mind and quietly reflect, testing the teaching in one's own conduct and in governance.

sentences.zh: 講官，令大臣公舉剛明正大之人，不拘官職大小。

translations.literal: As for lecturers, have high ministers jointly recommend men who are upright, clear, and magnanimous, without regard to the size of their offices.
translations.idiomatic: As for lecturers, have senior ministers jointly recommend men who are upright, clear, and magnanimous, without regard to the size of their offices.

sentences.zh: 一，公聽政。

translations.literal: Second, hear government openly.
translations.idiomatic: Second, hear government openly.

sentences.zh: 請日禦文華殿，午前進講，午後聽政。

translations.literal: I ask that Your Majesty hold court daily in the Wenhua Hall, lecture in the morning before noon, and hear government in the afternoon.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty hold court daily in Wenhua Hall, lecture in the morning, and hear government in the afternoon.

sentences.zh: 天下章奏，命諸臣詳議面陳可否，陛下親臨決其是非。

translations.literal: For memorials from all under Heaven, order the ministers to deliberate in detail and state face to face what is feasible or not; Your Majesty should personally decide right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: For memorials from across the realm, order ministers to deliberate in detail and state face to face what is feasible or not; Your Majesty should personally decide right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 暇則召五品以下官，隨意問以時事得失利病，令下情得以畢達。

translations.literal: In leisure, summon officials of the fifth grade and below and question them freely on the gains, losses, benefits, and harms of current affairs, so that sentiments below may be fully conveyed.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure, summon officials of the fifth grade and below and question them freely on the gains, losses, benefits, and harms of current affairs, so that sentiments below may be fully conveyed.

sentences.zh: 一，廣用賢。

translations.literal: Third, broadly employ the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Third, broadly employ the worthy.

sentences.zh: 請命給事中、御史，各陳兩京堂上官賢否。

translations.literal: I ask that supervising secretaries and censors each report whether the capital officials of the two capitals are worthy or not.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that supervising secretaries and censors each report whether the capital officials of the two capitals are worthy or not.

sentences.zh: 如有不盡，亦許在京五品官指陳之，以為進退。

translations.literal: If anything is incomplete, also allow capital officials of the fifth grade and below to point it out, as a basis for promotion and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: If anything is incomplete, also allow capital officials of the fifth grade and below to point it out, as a basis for promotion and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 又令共薦有德望者，以代所去之位，則大臣皆得其人。

translations.literal: Also have them jointly recommend men of virtue and reputation to fill vacated posts, so that high ministers will all obtain the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Also have them jointly recommend men of virtue and reputation to fill vacated posts, so that senior posts will be filled by the right men.

sentences.zh: 於是命之各言其所屬及方面郡縣官之賢否，付內閣吏部升黜之。

translations.literal: Thereupon order them each to speak of the worthiness or unworthiness of their subordinates and of regional, prefectural, and county officials, and refer this to the Grand Secretariat and Ministry of Personnel for promotion and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon order them each to report on the worthiness of their subordinates and of regional, prefectural, and county officials, and refer the reports to the Grand Secretariat and Ministry of Personnel for promotion and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 中外群臣，有剛正敢言者，舉為臺諫，不必論其言貌、官職、出身。

translations.literal: Among civil and military officials within and without, those who are upright and bold in speech should be recommended as censors and remonstrators, without regard to their speech, appearance, office, or background.
translations.idiomatic: Among officials within and without the capital, those who are upright and bold in speech should be recommended as censors and remonstrators, without regard to their speech, appearance, office, or background.

sentences.zh: 但不宜委之堂上官，恐憚其剛方，而薦柔媚者以充數，所舉之人感其推薦，不敢直斥其非。

translations.literal: But this should not be entrusted to capital officials, lest they fear the upright and recommend the soft and fawning to fill the quota; those recommended would be grateful for the recommendation and dare not directly criticize their faults.
translations.idiomatic: But this should not be entrusted to senior capital officials, lest they fear the upright and recommend the soft and fawning to fill the quota; those recommended would be grateful and dare not criticize their patrons.

sentences.zh: 是以古者大臣不舉臺諫。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity high ministers did not recommend censors and remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in antiquity senior ministers did not recommend censors and remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，以言多窒礙難行，寢之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, because its words were many and obstructive and hard to carry out, it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, the court found its proposals too obstructive to carry out and shelved it.

sentences.zh: 預修《英宗實錄》，與執政議不合，引疾家居，講求性命之學。

translations.literal: When he took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong, he disagreed with the chief ministers, cited illness, and lived at home, pursuing the learning of nature and destiny.
translations.idiomatic: While helping compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Yingzong, he disagreed with the chief ministers, cited illness, and lived at home, pursuing Neo-Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 閱二十年，中外交薦，皆不赴。

translations.literal: After twenty years, he was recommended from within and without the court, but he went on none of the summonses.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years he was recommended from within and without the court, but he accepted none of the summonses.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，召修《憲宗實錄》，進左贊善。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong and was promoted to Left Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong and was promoted to left mentor.

sentences.zh: 上言：「人君不以行王道為心，非大有為之主也。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "A ruler who does not take practicing the kingly way as his heart is not a ruler of great accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "A ruler who does not take practicing the kingly way as his heart is not a ruler of great accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 陛下毓德青宮，已負大有為之望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty cultivated virtue in the Eastern Palace and already bore the hope of great accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cultivated virtue in the Eastern Palace and already bore the hope of great accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 邇者頗崇異端，嬖近習，以蠱此心；

translations.literal: Recently you have rather honored heterodox teachings and favored close attendants, thereby bewitching this heart;
translations.idiomatic: Recently you have rather honored heterodox teachings and favored close attendants, thereby bewitching your heart;

sentences.zh: 殖貨利，耽玩好，以荒此心；

translations.literal: accumulated profit and goods and indulged in pleasures, thereby dissipating this heart;
translations.idiomatic: accumulated profit and indulged in pleasures, thereby dissipating your heart;

sentences.zh: 開幸門，塞言路，以昧此心。

translations.literal: opened the gate of favor and blocked the path of speech, thereby obscuring this heart.
translations.idiomatic: opened the gate of favor and blocked the path of remonstrance, thereby obscuring your heart.

sentences.zh: 則不能大有為矣。

translations.literal: Then you cannot accomplish greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Then you cannot accomplish greatly.

sentences.zh: 願定聖誌，一聖學，廣聖智。

translations.literal: I wish to fix the sagely will, unify sagely learning, and broaden sagely wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty fix your sagely resolve, unify your pursuit of sage learning, and broaden your sagely wisdom.

sentences.zh: 」疏反復累萬言，帝頗納之。

translations.literal: " The memorial, reiterated again and again, amounted to tens of thousands of words, and the emperor largely accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial, in repeated passages, ran to tens of thousands of words, and the emperor largely accepted it.

sentences.zh: 《實錄》成，遷南京侍講學士，以養母歸。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records were completed, he was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting in Nanjing and returned home to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records were completed, he was transferred to reader-in-waiting in Nanjing and went home to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為《會典》副總裁。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was summoned to serve as vice director of the Collected Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, he was summoned to serve as vice director of the Collected Statutes.

sentences.zh: 至則進學士，充經筵日講官，帝甚傾向。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was promoted to Hanlin Academician, appointed daily lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and the emperor was greatly inclined toward him.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival he was promoted to Hanlin academician and appointed daily lecturer at the Classics Colloquium; the emperor was deeply drawn to him.

sentences.zh: 元禎體清臒，長不逾中人，帝特設低幾聽之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen's physique was lean and ascetic, and his height did not exceed that of an average man; the emperor specially had a low lectern set for him to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen was spare and ascetic in build, no taller than an ordinary man, so the emperor had a low lectern specially set for him to hear the lectures.

sentences.zh: 數月，以母憂去。

translations.literal: Within a few months he left office on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，遷南京太常卿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 已，修《通鑒纂要》，復召為副總裁。

translations.literal: Thereafter, while compiling the Essence of the Comprehensive Mirror, he was again summoned as vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, while compiling the Essence of the Comprehensive Mirror, he was again summoned to serve as vice director.

sentences.zh: 以故官兼學士，改掌詹事府。

translations.literal: Retaining his former rank while also serving as academician, he was reassigned to head the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his former post while also serving as Hanlin academician, he was reassigned to head the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝晚年德益進。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor's virtue improved all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor's virtue advanced ever further.

sentences.zh: 元禎因請講筵增講《太極圖》、《通書》、《西銘》諸書。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen therefore requested that the Classics Colloquium additionally lecture on such works as Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Penetrating the Classic, and Western Inscription.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen therefore asked that the Classics Colloquium add lectures on such works as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Penetrating the Classic, and Western Inscription.

sentences.zh: 帝亟取觀之，喜曰：「天生斯人，以開朕也。

translations.literal: The emperor eagerly had them brought and read, and said with delight: "Heaven has born this man to enlighten me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor eagerly had them brought and read, and said with delight: "Heaven has born this man to enlighten me.

sentences.zh: 」欲大用之，未幾晏駕。

translations.literal: " He wished to employ him on a great scale, but before long the emperor passed away.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant to employ him on a grand scale, but before long the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，擢吏部左侍郎兼學士入東閣，專典誥敕。

translations.literal: When the Wuzong Emperor ascended the throne, he was promoted to Left Vice Minister of Personnel and Hanlin Academician, entered the Eastern Pavilion, and was charged exclusively with drafting edicts and commissions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong Emperor ascended the throne, Yuanzhen was promoted to left vice minister of Personnel and Hanlin academician, entered the Eastern Pavilion, and was charged exclusively with drafting edicts and commissions.

sentences.zh: 元禎素有盛譽。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen had long enjoyed great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen had long enjoyed great renown.

sentences.zh: 林居久，晚乃復出。

translations.literal: He had lived in retirement in the woods for a long time and only came forth again late in life.
translations.idiomatic: He had lived in woodland retirement for a long time and only returned to office late in life.

sentences.zh: 館閣諸人悉後輩，見元禎言論意態，以為迂闊，多姍笑之。

translations.literal: All those in the Hanlin halls were junior men; seeing Yuanzhen's speech and bearing, they regarded him as pedantic and impractical and often mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: All those in the Hanlin halls were junior men; seeing Yuanzhen's speech and bearing, they took him for pedantic and impractical and often mocked him.

sentences.zh: 又名位相軋，遂騰謗議，言官交章劾元禎。

translations.literal: Moreover, as fame and position jostled against one another, slander spread, and remonstrating officials submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as fame and rank pressed against one another, slander spread, and remonstrating officials submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 元禎七疏乞休，劉健力保持之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen submitted seven memorials begging to retire, and Liu Jian vigorously shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen submitted seven memorials begging to retire, and Liu Jian vigorously shielded him.

sentences.zh: 健去，元禎亦卒。

translations.literal: When Liu Jian departed, Yuanzhen also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jian left office, Yuanzhen also died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚文裕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously granted the title Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously granted the title Wenyu.

sentences.zh: 陳音，字師召，莆田人。

translations.literal: Chen Yin, style name Shizhao, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yin, whose style name was Shizhao, came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 天順末進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the late Tianshun reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the late Tianshun reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 成化六年三月，以災異陳時政，言：「講學莫先於好問。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Chenghua, citing calamities and portents he addressed current affairs and said: "In lecturing on learning, nothing comes before a love of questioning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year of Chenghua (1470), citing calamities and portents he addressed current affairs and said: "In lecturing on learning, nothing comes before a love of questioning.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖間禦經筵，然勢分嚴絕，上有疑未嘗問，下有見不敢陳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty occasionally attends the Classics Colloquium, yet the gulf of rank is severe; when you harbor doubts you never ask, and those below who see faults dare not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty occasionally attends the Classics Colloquium, yet the gulf of rank is severe; when you harbor doubts you never ask, and those below who see faults dare not speak.

sentences.zh: 願引儒臣賜坐便殿，從容咨論，仰發聖聰。

translations.literal: I wish that Confucian ministers be brought in and granted seats in an informal hall, that you may consult and discuss at leisure and thereby uplift your sagely understanding.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Confucian ministers be brought in and granted seats in an informal hall, that Your Majesty may consult and discuss at leisure and thereby uplift your sagely understanding.

sentences.zh: 異端者，正道之反，法王、佛子、真人，宜一切罷遣。

translations.literal: Heterodox teachings are the reverse of the right way; Dharma Kings, Buddhist sons, and True Men should all be dismissed without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Heterodox teachings are the reverse of the right way; Dharma Kings, Buddhist sons, and True Men should all be dismissed without exception.

sentences.zh: 」章下禮部。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 越數日，又奏：「國家養士百年，求其可用，不可多得。

translations.literal: Several days later he memorialized again: "The state has nurtured scholars for a century, yet among them few can be found fit for use.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he memorialized again: "The state has nurtured scholars for a century, yet among them few can be found fit for use.

sentences.zh: 如致仕尚書李秉，在籍修撰羅倫、編修張元禎、新會舉人陳獻章皆當世人望，宜召還秉等，而置獻章臺諫。

translations.literal: Such men as the retired Minister Li Bing, home-resident compiler Luo Lun, compiler Zhang Yuanzhen, and Xinhui licentiate Chen Xianzhang are all objects of public esteem in their day; Bing and the others should be recalled, and Xianzhang should be placed in a censorial or remonstrance post.
translations.idiomatic: Such men as the retired minister Li Bing, home-resident compiler Luo Lun, compiler Zhang Yuanzhen, and Xinhui licentiate Chen Xianzhang are all held in public esteem; Bing and the others should be recalled, and Xianzhang should be placed in a censorial or remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 言官多緘默，願召還判官王徽、評事章懋等，以開言路。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials are mostly silent; I wish that investigating censor Wang Hui, evaluating official Zhang Mao, and others be recalled to open the path of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials are mostly silent; I ask that investigating censor Wang Hui, evaluating official Zhang Mao, and others be recalled to open the path of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 」忤旨切責。

translations.literal: " This ran counter to the imperial will and brought sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: " This ran counter to the imperial will and brought sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 司禮太監黃賜母死，廷臣皆往吊，翰林不往。

translations.literal: When the Director of Ceremonial eunuch Huang Ci's mother died, court ministers all went to offer condolences, but the Hanlin did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the director of ceremonial eunuch Huang Ci's mother died, court ministers all went to offer condolences, but the Hanlin did not.

sentences.zh: 侍講徐瓊謀於眾，音大怒曰：「天子侍從臣，相率拜內豎之室，若清議何！

translations.literal: Reader-in-Waiting Xu Qiong plotted with the others, and Yin said in great anger: "Attendants of the Son of Heaven, going in a body to bow at an inner eunuch's house—what becomes of principled opinion!
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-waiting Xu Qiong plotted with the others, and Yin said in great anger: "Attendants of the Son of Heaven, going in a body to bow at an inner eunuch's house—what becomes of principled opinion!

sentences.zh: 」瓊愧沮。

translations.literal: " Qiong withdrew in shame and dejection.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiong withdrew in shame and dejection.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，進侍講。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 汪直黨韋瑛夜帥邏卒入兵部郎中楊士偉家，縛士偉，考掠及其妻子。

translations.literal: Wei Ying, a follower of Wang Zhi, led border troops by night into the home of Bureau Director Yang Shiwei of the Ministry of War, bound Shiwei, and tortured him along with his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ying, a follower of Wang Zhi, led border troops by night into the home of bureau director Yang Shiwei of the Ministry of War, bound Shiwei, and tortured him along with his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 音與比鄰，乘墉大呼曰：「爾擅辱朝臣，不畏國法耶！

translations.literal: Yin was a neighbor; he mounted the wall and shouted: "You dare insult a court minister without fear of the state's law!
translations.idiomatic: Yin was a neighbor; he mounted the wall and shouted: "You dare insult a court minister without fear of the state's law!

sentences.zh: 」其人曰：「爾何人，不畏西廠！

translations.literal: " The man said: "Who are you—do you not fear the Western Depot!
translations.idiomatic: " The man said: "Who are you—do you not fear the Western Depot!

sentences.zh: 」音厲聲曰：「我翰林陳音也。

translations.literal: " Yin said in a harsh voice: "I am Chen Yin of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin said in a harsh voice: "I am Chen Yin of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 」久之，遷南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: " After a long while he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long while he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 劉吉父喪起復，音貽書勸其固辭，吉不悅。

translations.literal: When Liu Ji left mourning early to resume office after his father's death, Yin sent him a letter urging him firmly to decline; Ji was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Ji left mourning early to resume office after his father's death, Yin sent him a letter urging him firmly to decline; Ji was displeased.

sentences.zh: 後吏部擬用音，吉輒阻之曰「腐儒」，以故十年不得調。

translations.literal: Later, when the Ministry of Personnel proposed to employ Yin, Ji always blocked it, calling him "a rotten pedant," and for this reason Yin went ten years without a transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Ministry of Personnel proposed to employ Yin, Ji always blocked it, calling him "a rotten pedant," and for this reason Yin went ten years without a transfer.

sentences.zh: 嘗與守備中官爭事，為所劾，事卒得直。

translations.literal: Once he disputed a matter with a garrison eunuch and was impeached by him, but in the end the case was decided in his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Once he disputed a matter with a garrison eunuch and was impeached by him, but in the end the case was decided in his favor.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，吉罷，始進本寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, when Ji was dismissed, Yin was at last promoted to Director of his bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi (1492), when Ji was dismissed, Yin was at last promoted to director of his bureau.

sentences.zh: 越二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 音負經術，士多遊其門者。

translations.literal: Yin was steeped in the classics; many scholars associated with his school.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was steeped in the classics, and many scholars studied under him.

sentences.zh: 然性健忘，世故瑣屑事皆不解。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was forgetful and understood none of the petty affairs of worldly life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was forgetful and understood none of the petty affairs of worldly life.

sentences.zh: 世多以不慧事附之以為笑，然不盡實也。

translations.literal: The world often attached tales of his lack of wit to make sport of him, yet these are not wholly true.
translations.idiomatic: The world often attached tales of his lack of wit to make sport of him, yet these are not wholly true.

sentences.zh: 傅瀚，字曰川，新喻人。

translations.literal: Fu Han, style name Yuechuan, was a native of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Han, whose style name was Yuechuan, came from Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 天順八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tianshun (1464).

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，除檢討。

translations.literal: Selected as Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 嗜學強記，善詩文。

translations.literal: Devoted to learning with a powerful memory, he excelled at poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to learning with a powerful memory, he excelled at poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 再遷左諭德，直講東宮。

translations.literal: Promoted again to Left Preceptor, he lectured directly in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted again to left preceptor, he lectured directly in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，擢太常少卿兼侍讀，歷禮部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, and served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiaozong Emperor succeeded, he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent reader-in-waiting, and served as left and right vice minister of Rites.
