sentences.zh: 尋命兼學士入東閣，專典誥敕，兼掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve concurrently as academician in the Eastern Pavilion, charged exclusively with drafting edicts and commissions, and also to administer the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to serve concurrently as Hanlin academician in the Eastern Pavilion, charged exclusively with drafting edicts and commissions, and also to administer the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年代徐瓊為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi he replaced Xu Qiong as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Hongzhi (1500) he replaced Xu Qiong as minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 保定獻白鵲，疏斥之。

translations.literal: When Baoding presented a white magpie, he memorialized condemning it.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoding presented a white magpie, he memorialized condemning the offering.

sentences.zh: 陜西巡撫熊翀以鄠縣民所得玉璽來獻，以為秦璽復出也。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Xiong Chong presented a jade seal obtained by a commoner in Hu County, believing the Qin imperial seal had reappeared.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi grand coordinator Xiong Chong presented a jade seal obtained by a commoner in Hu County, believing the Qin imperial seal had reappeared.

sentences.zh: 瀚率同列言：「秦璽完毀，具載簡冊。

translations.literal: Han led his colleagues in saying: "The Qin seal was completely destroyed; this is fully recorded in the annals.
translations.idiomatic: Han led his colleagues in saying: "The Qin seal was completely destroyed; this is fully recorded in the annals.

sentences.zh: 今所進璽，形色、篆紐皆不類，蓋後人仿為之。

translations.literal: The seal now presented differs in form, color, and seal script and knob—it is clearly a later imitation.
translations.idiomatic: The seal now presented differs in form, color, and seal script and knob—it is clearly a later imitation.

sentences.zh: 且帝王受命在德不在璽，太祖制六璽，列聖相承，百三十餘載，天休滋至，受命之符不在秦璽明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, emperors receive the Mandate through virtue, not through a seal; the Founding Emperor fashioned six seals, successive sage rulers have handed them down for more than a hundred and thirty years, Heaven's favor has ever increased—the token of the Mandate plainly does not lie in the Qin seal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, emperors receive the Mandate through virtue, not through a seal; the Founding Emperor fashioned six seals, successive sage rulers have handed them down for more than a hundred and thirty years, Heaven's favor has ever increased—the token of the Mandate plainly does not lie in the Qin seal.

sentences.zh: 請姑藏內府。

translations.literal: I ask that it be stored for the time being in the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that it be stored for the time being in the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 」帝是其言，薄賞得璽者。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his view and gave a modest reward to the man who had obtained the seal.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his view and gave a modest reward to the man who had obtained the seal.

sentences.zh: 京師星變、地震、雨雹，四方多變異。

translations.literal: In the capital there were changes in the stars, earthquakes, and hail; throughout the realm portents multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital there were changes in the stars, earthquakes, and hail; throughout the realm portents multiplied.

sentences.zh: 瀚條上軍民所不便進者，請躬行節儉以先天下。

translations.literal: Han itemized what army and people found burdensome to submit and asked that the emperor personally practice frugality to lead the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Han itemized what army and people found burdensome to submit and asked that the emperor personally practice frugality to lead the empire.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺逋行戶物價至四萬餘兩。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments owed market households more than forty thousand taels in goods prices.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments owed market households more than forty thousand taels in goods prices.

sentences.zh: 瀚言由供億之濫，願敦儉素，俾冗費不生。

translations.literal: Han said this arose from wasteful provisioning and wished to promote plain living so that superfluous expenses would not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Han said this arose from wasteful provisioning and wished to promote plain living so that superfluous expenses would not arise.

sentences.zh: 所條奏，率傅正議。

translations.literal: The items he memorialized mostly spread forth upright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The items he memorialized mostly upheld principled counsel.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒，贈太子太保，謚文穆。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and granted the posthumous title Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1502) he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand mentor of the Heir Apparent and granted the posthumous title Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 張昇，字啟昭，南城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng, style name Qizhao, was a native of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng, whose style name was Qizhao, came from Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士第一。

translations.literal: He took first place in the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chenghua (1469).

sentences.zh: 授修撰，歷諭德。

translations.literal: Appointed compiler, he served as preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed compiler, he served as preceptor.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元，遷庶子。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi began a new reign era, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhi began a new reign era, he was transferred to vice director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉吉當國，昇因天變，疏言：「陛下即位，言者率以萬安、劉吉、尹直為言，安、直被斥，吉獨存。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Ji held power; Sheng, citing heavenly portents, memorialized: "Since Your Majesty's accession, critics have generally singled out Wan An, Liu Ji, and Yin Zhi; An and Zhi were dismissed, but Ji alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Ji held power; Sheng, citing heavenly portents, memorialized: "Since Your Majesty's accession, critics have generally singled out Wan An, Liu Ji, and Yin Zhi; An and Zhi were dismissed, but Ji alone remained.

sentences.zh: 吉乃傾身阿佞，取悅言官，昏暮款門，祈免糾劾，許以超遷。

translations.literal: Ji then threw himself into fawning flattery, seeking to please remonstrating officials; at dusk he would knock at their doors, praying to escape impeachment and promising rapid promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Ji then threw himself into fawning flattery, seeking to please remonstrating officials; at dusk he would knock at their doors, praying to escape impeachment and promising rapid promotion.

sentences.zh: 由是諫官緘口，奸計始遂。

translations.literal: By this means the remonstrators fell silent, and his wicked schemes succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: By this means the remonstrators fell silent, and his wicked schemes succeeded.

sentences.zh: 貴戚萬喜依憑宮壺，凶焰熾張，吉與締姻。

translations.literal: The imperial kinsman Wan Xi relied on the inner palace women; his violent arrogance blazed, and Ji contracted a marriage alliance with him.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial kinsman Wan Xi relied on the inner palace women; his violent arrogance blazed, and Ji contracted a marriage alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 及喜下獄，猶為營救。

translations.literal: When Xi was thrown into prison, Ji still worked to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was thrown into prison, Ji still worked to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 父存則異居各爨，父歿則奪情起官。

translations.literal: While his father lived he lived apart and kept separate kitchens; when his father died he left mourning early to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: While his father lived he lived apart and kept separate kitchens; when his father died he left mourning early to resume office.

sentences.zh: 談笑對客，無復戚容。

translations.literal: He chatted and laughed with guests and showed no grief.
translations.idiomatic: He chatted and laughed with guests and showed no grief.

sentences.zh: 盛納艷姬，恣為淫黷。

translations.literal: He kept many beautiful concubines and indulged in lewd excess.
translations.idiomatic: He kept many beautiful concubines and indulged in lewd excess.

sentences.zh: 」且歷數其納賄、縱子等十罪。

translations.literal: " He also enumerated ten crimes, including accepting bribes and indulging his sons.
translations.idiomatic: " He also enumerated ten crimes, including accepting bribes and indulging his sons.

sentences.zh: 吉憤甚，風科道劾昇誣詆，調南京工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Ji was furious; he prompted the censorial officials to impeach Sheng for slander, and Sheng was transferred to Assistant Department Director in the Ministry of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was furious; he prompted the censorial officials to impeach Sheng for slander, and Sheng was transferred to assistant department director in the Ministry of Works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 吉罷，復故官，歷禮部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: When Ji was dismissed, Sheng returned to his former post and served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji was dismissed, Sheng returned to his former post and served as left and right vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十五年代傅瀚為尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he replaced Fu Han as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1502) he replaced Fu Han as minister.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，真人陳應衤盾、西番灌頂大國師那卜堅參等以祓除，率其徒入乾清宮，昇請置之法。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died, the True Man Chen Yingxiang, the Tibetan anointment grand state preceptor Napojianzan, and others entered the Palace of Heavenly Purity to perform purification rites, leading their followers; Sheng requested that they be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong died, the True Man Chen Yingxiang, the Tibetan anointment grand state preceptor Napojianzan, and others entered the Palace of Heavenly Purity to perform purification rites, leading their followers; Sheng requested that they be punished by law.

sentences.zh: 詔奪真人、國師、高士等三十餘人名號，逐之。

translations.literal: An edict stripped more than thirty True Men, state preceptors, lofty masters, and the like of their titles and expelled them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped more than thirty True Men, state preceptors, lofty masters, and the like of their titles and expelled them.

sentences.zh: 昇在部五年，遇災異，輒進直言。

translations.literal: Sheng was in the ministry five years; whenever portents occurred he promptly submitted forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was in the ministry five years; whenever portents occurred he promptly submitted forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 亦數為言者所攻，然自守謹飭。

translations.literal: He was also often attacked by remonstrators, yet he kept himself strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He was also often attacked by remonstrators, yet he kept himself strict and orderly.

sentences.zh: 武宗嬉遊怠政，給事中胡煜、楊一渶、張襘皆以為言，章下禮部。

translations.literal: The Wuzong Emperor played and neglected government; supervising secretaries Hu Yu, Yang Yihao, and Zhang Gui all spoke out; their memorials were sent to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuzong Emperor played and neglected government; supervising secretaries Hu Yu, Yang Yihao, and Zhang Gui all spoke out; their memorials were sent to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 昇因上疏，請親賢遠佞，克謹天戒。

translations.literal: Sheng therefore submitted a memorial asking to cherish the worthy and keep the flatterers at a distance, and to heed heaven's warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng therefore submitted a memorial asking to cherish the worthy and keep flatterers at a distance, and to heed heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 帝是之而不能用，昇遂連疏乞休，不允。

translations.literal: The emperor approved but could not act on it; Sheng then submitted memorial after memorial begging to retire, without success.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved but could not act on it; Sheng then submitted memorial after memorial begging to retire, without success.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，秦府鎮國將軍誠漖請襲封保安王，昇執不可。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, the Defending State General of the Princedom of Qin, Chengji, requested inheritance of the title Prince of Bao'an; Sheng firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde (1507), the defending state general of the Princedom of Qin, Chengji, requested inheritance of the title Prince of Bao'an; Sheng firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 忤劉瑾，謝病。

translations.literal: Offending Liu Jin, he pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Offending Liu Jin, he pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太保，乘傳歸，月米、歲夫如制。

translations.literal: An edict added the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; he returned home by post carriage with monthly grain and annual corvée laborers as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added the title grand mentor of the Heir Apparent; he returned home by post carriage with monthly grain and annual corvée laborers as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 吳寬，字原博，長洲人。

translations.literal: Wu Kuan, style name Yuanbo, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kuan, whose style name was Yuanbo, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 以文行有聲諸生間。

translations.literal: Through literary conduct he had a reputation among the student scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His learning and personal conduct won him renown among fellow students.

sentences.zh: 成化八年，會試、廷試皆第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua, he placed first in both the metropolitan and palace examinations and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Chenghua reign (1472), he topped both the metropolitan and palace examinations and was appointed a reviser at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 侍孝宗東宮，秩滿進右諭德。

translations.literal: He served in the Eastern Palace of Emperor Xiaozong; when his term expired he was promoted to Right Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He attended Prince Xiaozong in the Eastern Palace, and when his term ended was promoted to right sub-reader.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，以舊學遷左庶子，預修《憲宗實錄》，進少詹事兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, on account of his old tutelage he was transferred to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent while also serving as Reader and Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong came to the throne, he was moved to left assistant to the heir apparent as a former tutor, took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong, and was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent while retaining his posts as reader and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年擢吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Hongzhi reign (1495), he was promoted to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，吏部員缺，命虛位待之。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his stepmother, the post at the Ministry of Personnel fell vacant, and he was ordered to leave the position open and wait for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his stepmother, the Ministry of Personnel post was left vacant by imperial order until he could return.

sentences.zh: 服滿還任，轉左，改掌詹事府，入東閣，專典誥敕，仍侍武宗東宮。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to office, was transferred to the left post, reassigned to head the Household of the Heir Apparent, entered the Eastern Lodge, was put exclusively in charge of edicts and patents, and still attended Prince Wuzong in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was over he resumed office, moved to the left vice ministership, took charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent, entered the Eastern Lodge to handle edicts and patents exclusively, and continued to attend Prince Wuzong in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 宦豎多不欲太子近儒臣，數移事間講讀。

translations.literal: Eunuchs mostly did not want the crown prince near Confucian ministers, and repeatedly interposed other business to interrupt the lectures.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs mostly did not want the crown prince close to Confucian tutors, and repeatedly used other duties to interrupt his lectures.

sentences.zh: 寬率其僚上疏曰：「東宮講學，寒暑風雨則止，朔望令節則止，一年不過數月，一月不過數日，一日不過數刻。

translations.literal: Kuan led his colleagues in submitting a memorial saying: "Lectures in the Eastern Palace cease in cold, heat, wind, and rain, and cease on the first and fifteenth of the month and on festival days; in a year there are no more than a few months, in a month no more than a few days, and in a day no more than a few quarters of an hour.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan led his colleagues in submitting a memorial: "Lectures in the Eastern Palace stop for cold, heat, wind, and rain, and stop on the new and full moon and on festival days; in a year there are at most a few months of instruction, in a month at most a few days, and in a day at most a few brief sessions.

sentences.zh: 是進講之時少，輟講之日多，豈容復以他事妨誦讀。

translations.literal: Thus the time for advancing lectures is little and the days when lectures stop are many—how can it be permitted that other affairs again obstruct recitation and study?
translations.idiomatic: Time spent lecturing is therefore little and days without lectures are many—how can other business be allowed to obstruct study yet again?

sentences.zh: 古人八歲就傅，即居宿於外，欲離近習，親正人耳。

translations.literal: In antiquity, at eight one received a tutor and immediately lived and lodged outside, wishing to leave close associates and draw near upright men—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a child of eight took a tutor and lodged apart from home, precisely to leave bad company and keep company with upright men.

sentences.zh: 庶民且然，矧太子天下本哉？

translations.literal: Even common people were so—how much more so the crown prince, the foundation of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Even commoners did this—how much more so the crown prince, upon whom the realm itself depends?

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the memorial and accepted its advice.

sentences.zh: 十六年進禮部尚書，余如故。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Rites; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to minister of rites; his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 先是，孝莊錢太后崩，廷議孝肅周太后萬歲後，並葬裕陵，祔睿廟，禮皆如適。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Dowager Qian of Xiaozhuang died, the court debated that after Empress Dowager Zhou of Xiaosu passed away she should be buried together at Yuling and enshrined in the temple of Emperor Ruizong, with rites all as for the primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Empress Dowager Qian of Xiaozhuang died, the court had debated that after Empress Dowager Zhou of Xiaosu passed away she should be buried with the emperor at Yuling, enshrined in the temple of Emperor Ruizong, and accorded rites equal to those of the principal consort.

sentences.zh: 至是，孝肅崩，將祔廟，帝終以並祔為疑，下禮官集議。

translations.literal: At this point Xiaosu died; as she was to be enshrined in the temple, the emperor still had doubts about joint enshrinement and ordered the ritual officials to assemble for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaosu died and the time came to enshrine her in the ancestral temple, the emperor still doubted joint enshrinement and ordered the ritual officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 寬言《魯頌·宮》、《春秋》考仲子之宮皆別廟，漢、唐亦然。

translations.literal: Kuan said that in "Gong" in the Lu Eulogies and in the Spring and Autumn Annals the temple of Zhongzi was a separate temple, and Han and Tang were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan argued that the "Gong" ode in the Lu Eulogies and the Spring and Autumn Annals' account of Zhongzi's separate temple both prescribed separate shrines, as did Han and Tang practice.

sentences.zh: 會大臣亦多主別廟，帝乃從之。

translations.literal: As it happened, many high ministers also advocated a separate temple, and the emperor then followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Many senior ministers also favored a separate shrine, and the emperor accepted their view.

sentences.zh: 時詞臣望重者，寬為最，謝遷次之。

translations.literal: Among literary officials of heavy repute at the time, Kuan ranked first and Xie Qian second.
translations.idiomatic: Among the most esteemed literary officials of the day, Kuan stood first and Xie Qian second.

sentences.zh: 遷既入閣，嘗為劉健言，欲引寬共政，健固不從。

translations.literal: Once Qian had entered the Grand Secretariat, he once told Liu Jian that he wished to bring Kuan in to share governance, but Jian firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian entered the Grand Secretariat, he once told Liu Jian that he wished to bring Kuan into the cabinet to share power, but Jian firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 他日又曰：「吳公科第、年齒、聞望皆先於遷，遷實自愧，豈有私於吳公耶。

translations.literal: Another day he said again: "Lord Wu's examination rank, age, and reputation all precede Qian's; Qian truly feels ashamed—how could there be partiality toward Lord Wu?
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he said: "Lord Wu's rank, age, and reputation all precede my own; I truly feel ashamed before him—how could I show favoritism toward him?

sentences.zh: 」及遷引退，舉寬自代，亦不果用。

translations.literal: " When Qian retired and recommended Kuan to succeed him, this too was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " When Qian retired and recommended Kuan to succeed him, that recommendation too went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 中外皆為之惜，而寬甚安之，曰：「吾初望不及此也。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court all regretted it for him, but Kuan was quite at ease and said: "My early hopes did not reach this far.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike regretted the missed appointment, but Kuan was entirely at peace and said: "My early ambitions never reached this far.

sentences.zh: 」年七十，數引疾，輒慰留，竟卒於官。

translations.literal: " At seventy he repeatedly cited illness, but each time was comforted and retained; in the end he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: " At seventy he repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of illness, but each time the emperor comforted him and kept him on; he died in office at last.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as grand mentor of the heir apparent and given the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: 授長子奭中書舍人，補次子奐國子生，異數也。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yi was appointed secretary in the Secretariat-Chancellery, and his second son Huan was enrolled as a student at the National University—exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yi was appointed a secretariat secretary, and his second son Huan was enrolled as a student at the Imperial Academy—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 寬行履高潔，不為激矯，而自守以正。

translations.literal: Kuan's conduct was lofty and pure; he did not affect exaggeration but upheld himself with rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's conduct was lofty and unsullied; he did not affect moral display, but held himself upright by principle.

sentences.zh: 於書無不讀，詩文有典則，兼工書法。

translations.literal: There was no book he did not read; his poetry and prose had classical norms, and he was also skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in every field, wrote poetry and prose with classical restraint, and was also accomplished in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 有田數頃，嘗以周親故之貧者。

translations.literal: He had several qing of land and often used it to help impoverished relatives and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: He owned several qing of land and often used the income to support impoverished relatives and old friends.

sentences.zh: 友人賀恩疾，遷至邸，旦夕視之。

translations.literal: When his friend He En fell ill, he moved to his residence and visited morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend He En fell ill, he moved into his house and attended him morning and night.

sentences.zh: 恩死，為衣素一月。

translations.literal: When En died, he wore plain white mourning for a month.
translations.idiomatic: When En died, he wore plain white mourning for a full month.

sentences.zh: 傅珪，字邦瑞，清苑人。

translations.literal: Fu Gui, style name Bangrui, was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gui, whose style name was Bangrui, came from Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-third year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil examinations as a jinshi in the twenty-third year of the Chenghua reign (1487).

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was made a probationary palace scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a probationary palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，授編修，尋兼司經局校書。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi he was appointed compiler and soon also served concurrently as collator in the Directorate of Classics.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he was appointed a compiler and soon also served as collator in the Directorate of Classics.

sentences.zh: 與修《大明會典》成，遷左中允。

translations.literal: When compilation of the Da Ming Collected Statutes was completed, he was promoted to Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Da Ming Collected Statutes were completed, he was promoted to left assistant director.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，以東宮恩，進左諭德，充講官，纂修《孝宗實錄》。

translations.literal: When Wuzong came to the throne, through Eastern Palace favor he was promoted to Left Sub-Reader, served as lecturer, and helped compile the Veritable Records of Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to left sub-reader through his former service in the Eastern Palace, served as a lecturer, and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 時詞臣不附劉瑾，瑾惡之。

translations.literal: At the time literary officials did not attach themselves to Liu Jin, and Jin hated them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the literary officials would not attach themselves to Liu Jin, and Jin hated them for it.

sentences.zh: 謂《會典》成於劉健等，多所糜費，鐫與修者官，降珪修撰。

translations.literal: Claiming that the Collected Statutes had been completed under Liu Jian and others with much waste, offices of those who compiled it were struck from the rolls, and Gui was demoted to reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Jin claimed that the Collected Statutes compiled under Liu Jian and others had wasted vast sums, struck the offices of those who had compiled it, and demoted Gui to reviser.

sentences.zh: 俄以《實錄》成，進左中允，再遷翰林學士，歷吏部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon, when the Veritable Records were completed, he was promoted to Left Assistant Director, then again to Hanlin Academician, and served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when the Veritable Records were completed, he was promoted to left assistant director, then to Hanlin academician, and served successively as left and right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 正德六年，代費宏為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he replaced Fei Hong as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhengde reign (1511), he replaced Fei Hong as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 禮部事視他部為簡，自珪數有執爭，章奏遂多。

translations.literal: The affairs of the Ministry of Rites were simpler than those of other ministries, but from Gui's time there were repeated firm disputes, and memorials therefore grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites had lighter duties than other ministries, but from Gui's tenure onward its firm disputes with the throne made memorials multiply.

sentences.zh: 帝好佛，自稱「大慶法王」。

translations.literal: The emperor favored Buddhism and styled himself "Dharma King of Great Celebration."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored Buddhism and styled himself the "Dharma King of Great Celebration."

sentences.zh: 番僧乞田百頃為法王下院，中旨下部，稱大慶法王與聖旨並。

translations.literal: A Tibetan monk requested a hundred qing of land for a subsidiary monastery of the Dharma King; an imperial rescript descended to the ministry, placing the Dharma King of Great Celebration on a par with the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: A Tibetan monk requested a hundred qing of land for a subsidiary monastery of the dharma king; an imperial rescript reached the ministry placing the Dharma King of Great Celebration on equal footing with the throne's own edict.

sentences.zh: 珪佯不知，執奏：「孰為大慶法王？

translations.literal: Gui feigned ignorance and submitted a firm memorial: "Who is the Dharma King of Great Celebration?
translations.idiomatic: Gui feigned ignorance and submitted a firm memorial: "Who is this Dharma King of Great Celebration?

sentences.zh: 敢與至尊並書，大不敬。

translations.literal: To dare place him on equal footing with the sovereign in writing is gross disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: To place him on equal footing with the sovereign in writing is gross disrespect.

sentences.zh: 」詔勿問，田亦竟止。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued, and the land grant was ultimately stopped as well.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered that the matter not be pursued, and the land grant was stopped in the end.

sentences.zh: 珪居閑類木訥者。

translations.literal: In repose Gui seemed like a dull, slow-spoken man.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times Gui seemed dull and slow of speech.

sentences.zh: 及當大事，毅然執持，人不能奪，卒以此忤權幸去。

translations.literal: But when great affairs were at stake he held firm with resolve that no one could sway, and in the end was removed for this reason after offending the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: But when great affairs were at stake he held firm with a resolve no one could shake, and in the end lost office for offending the powerful favorites.

sentences.zh: 教坊司臧賢請易牙牌，制如朝士，又請改鑄方印。

translations.literal: Zang Xian of the Music Bureau requested replacement of tally-plaques, with the design like those of court officials, and also requested recasting of a square seal.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xian of the Music Bureau asked to replace his tally-plaques with ones like those of court officials, and also requested a newly cast square seal.

sentences.zh: 珪格不行。

translations.literal: Gui blocked it and would not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Gui blocked both requests and refused to carry them out.

sentences.zh: 賢日夜騰謗於諸閹間，冀去珪。

translations.literal: Xian day and night spread slander among the eunuchs, hoping to remove Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Xian spent day and night spreading slander among the eunuchs, hoping to drive Gui from office.

sentences.zh: 流寇擾河南，太監陸訚謀督師，下廷議，莫敢先發。

translations.literal: Roaming bandits troubled Henan; the eunuch Lu Yan plotted to take overall command; the matter was sent down for court debate, and no one dared speak first.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming bandits ravaged Henan; the eunuch Lu Yan sought overall command of the campaign; the matter was sent to court for debate, and no one dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 珪厲聲曰：「師老民疲，賊日熾，以冒功者多，僨事者漏罰，失將士心。

translations.literal: Gui said in a stern voice: "The army is worn and the people exhausted; the bandits grow fiercer by the day; many claim credit falsely while those who ruin affairs escape punishment—this loses the hearts of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Gui said sharply: "The army is worn out and the people exhausted; the bandits grow fiercer by the day; many claim false credit while those who ruin campaigns escape punishment—this destroys the morale of officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 先所遣已無功，可復遣耶？

translations.literal: Those previously dispatched achieved nothing—can they be sent again?
translations.idiomatic: The commanders already sent have achieved nothing—can we send them out again?

sentences.zh: 今賊橫行郊圻肘腋間，民囂然思亂，禍旦夕及宗社。

translations.literal: Now the bandits roam freely in the outskirts and at the emperor's very side; the people clamor with thoughts of revolt, and disaster may reach the altars of state any day.
translations.idiomatic: Now the bandits roam the capital's outskirts and even its very gates; the people clamor with thoughts of revolt, and disaster may strike the altars of state at any moment.

sentences.zh: 吾儕死不償責，諸公安得首鼠兩端。

translations.literal: We would not pay with our deaths for our responsibilities—how can you gentlemen hesitate like a rat with two burrows?
translations.idiomatic: Even our deaths would not discharge our responsibility—how can you gentlemen sit on the fence like rats with two holes?

sentences.zh: 」由是議罷。

translations.literal: " Because of this the plan was dropped in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " On that basis the proposal was dropped in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 疏上，竟遣訚，而中官皆憾珪。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, Yan was nevertheless dispatched, and all the inner officials resented Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Yan was dispatched anyway, and the inner officials all resented Gui.

sentences.zh: 御史張羽奏雲南災。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Yu memorialized on disasters in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Yu memorialized about disasters in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 珪因極言四方災變可畏。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon spoke at length that calamities and portents in all directions were to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Gui thereupon spoke at length about the alarming calamities and portents appearing in every direction.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，復奏四月災，因言：「春秋二百四十二年，災變六十九事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he again memorialized on the disasters of the fourth month, saying: "In the 242 years of the Spring and Autumn period there were sixty-nine cases of calamity and portent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year he again memorialized about the disasters of the fourth month, saying: "In the 242 years covered by the Spring and Autumn Annals there were only sixty-nine recorded calamities and portents.

sentences.zh: 今自去秋來，地震天鳴，雹降星殞，龍虎出見，地裂山崩，凡四十有二，而水旱不與焉，災未有若是甚者。

translations.literal: From last autumn until now there have been earthquakes, sky-thunder, hail, falling stars, dragons and tigers appearing, earth splitting and mountains collapsing—forty-two in all, not counting floods and droughts; never have calamities been so severe.
translations.idiomatic: Since last autumn alone there have been earthquakes, thunder in a clear sky, hail, falling stars, dragons and tigers appearing, earth splitting and mountains collapsing—forty-two in all, not counting floods and droughts; never have calamities been so severe.

sentences.zh: 」極陳時弊十事，語多斥權幸，權幸益深嫉之。

translations.literal: " He set forth ten current abuses at length, his words largely censuring the powerful and favored, who therefore hated him all the more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: " He then set forth ten current abuses at length, his words largely censuring the powerful favorites, who hated him all the more deeply for it.

sentences.zh: 會戶部尚書孫交亦以守正見忤，遂矯旨令二人致仕。

translations.literal: As it happened Minister of Revenue Sun Jiao had also offended by upholding rectitude, and a forged edict then ordered the two men to retire.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened Minister of Revenue Sun Jiao had also offended the throne by upholding rectitude, and a forged edict then ordered both men to retire.

sentences.zh: 兩京言官交章請留，不聽。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials in both capitals submitted successive memorials asking that they be kept, but this was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials in both capitals submitted successive memorials asking that the two be retained, but the throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 珪歸三年，御史盧雍稱珪在位有古大臣風，家無儲蓄，日給為累，乞頒月廩、歲隸，以示優禮。

translations.literal: Three years after Gui returned home, Censor Lu Yong praised Gui's conduct in office as having the bearing of an ancient great minister, that his household had no savings and daily sustenance was a burden, and asked that monthly grain and annual retainers be granted to show special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after Gui retired, Censor Lu Yong praised his conduct in office as having the bearing of the great ministers of old, noted that his household had no savings and daily living was a burden, and asked that monthly grain and annual retainers be granted as a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 又謂珪剛直忠讜，當起用。

translations.literal: He also said that Gui was upright, frank, and loyal in remonstrance and ought to be reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Gui was upright, frank, and loyal in remonstrance and ought to be recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 吏部請如雍言，不報。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel requested acting as Yong had said; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel requested acting on Yong's proposal, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 而珪適卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Gui happened to die just then, at fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Gui happened to die just then, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 遣命毋請恤典。

translations.literal: His final instructions were not to request mourning honors.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions were that no posthumous honors be requested.

sentences.zh: 撫、按以為言，詔蔭其子中書舍人。

translations.literal: The provincial governor and surveillance commissioner spoke on his behalf, and an edict ennobled his son as secretary in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor and surveillance commissioner appealed on his behalf, and an edict granted his son the post of secretariat secretary by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年錄先朝守正大臣，追贈太子少保，謚文毅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing, as upright ministers of the former reign were recorded, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jiajing reign (1522), when upright ministers of the previous reign were honored, he was posthumously enfeoffed as junior guardian of the heir apparent and given the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 劉春，字仁仲，巴人。

translations.literal: Liu Chun, style name Renzhong, was a native of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chun, whose style name was Renzhong, came from Ba.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年進士及第。

translations.literal: A palace graduate jinshi of the twenty-third year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination as a jinshi in the twenty-third year of the Chenghua reign (1487).

sentences.zh: 授編修，屢遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: Appointed compiler, he was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed a compiler, he was repeatedly promoted until he reached Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 正德六年擢吏部右侍郎，進左。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel, then to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhengde reign (1511) he was promoted to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then to the left post.

sentences.zh: 八年代傅珪為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he replaced Fu Gui as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he replaced Fu Gui as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 淮王祐棨、鄭王祐檡皆由旁支襲封，而祐棨稱其本生為考，祐檡並欲追封入廟。

translations.literal: Princes Youqi of Huai and Youji of Zheng both inherited their fiefs from collateral lines, yet Youqi called his biological father "father," and Youji also wished to posthumously enfeoff him and install him in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Youqi of Huai and Youji of Zheng had both inherited their titles from collateral lines, yet Youqi called his biological father "father," and Youji also sought posthumous enfeoffment and installation in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 交城王秉杋由鎮國將軍嗣爵，而進其妹為縣主。

translations.literal: Prince Bingfang of Jiaocheng succeeded to the title from National Guardian General rank and promoted his younger sister to county princess.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bingfang of Jiaocheng had succeeded to the title from the rank of state guardian general and sought to elevate his younger sister to county princess.

sentences.zh: 春皆據禮駁之，遂著為例。

translations.literal: Chun rejected all these on grounds of ritual and they were established as precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Chun rejected all these petitions on ritual grounds, and his rulings were established as precedents.

sentences.zh: 帝崇信西僧，常襲其衣服，演法內廠。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply believed in Western monks, often wore their garb, and expounded the dharma at the Inner Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply trusted Western monks, often wore their robes, and preached the dharma at the Inner Works.

sentences.zh: 有綽吉我些兒者，出入豹房，封大德法王。

translations.literal: There was one called Chuoji Wo Xie'er who went in and out of the Leopard Quarter and was enfeoffed as Great Virtue Dharma King.
translations.idiomatic: One monk named Chuoji Wo Xie'er moved freely in and out of the Leopard Quarter and was enfeoffed as the Great Virtue Dharma King.

sentences.zh: 遣其徒二人還烏思藏，請給國師誥命如大乘法王例，歲時入貢，且得賫茶以行。

translations.literal: He sent two disciples back to U-Tsang to request a State Preceptor patent of appointment on the model of the Great Vehicle Dharma King, yearly tribute missions, and permission to carry tea as imperial gift for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: He sent two disciples back to U-Tsang to request a state preceptor patent on the model granted the Great Vehicle Dharma King, yearly tribute missions, and permission to carry imperial tribute tea for the journey.

sentences.zh: 春持不可。

translations.literal: Chun maintained it could not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Chun maintained that this could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 帝命再議，春執奏曰：「烏思藏遠在西方，性極頑獷。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered further deliberation; Chun submitted a firm memorial saying: "U-Tsang lies far in the west; its nature is extremely stubborn and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered further deliberation; Chun submitted a firm memorial: "U-Tsang lies far in the west, and its people are by nature extremely stubborn and fierce.

sentences.zh: 雖設四王撫化，其來貢必有節制，使不為邊患。

translations.literal: Although four kings were established to pacify and transform them, their coming to tribute must have limits so that they do not become a border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Although four kings were established to pacify and convert them, their tribute missions must be strictly limited so that they do not become a border menace.

sentences.zh: 若許其賫茶，給之誥敕，萬一假上旨以誘羌人，妄有請乞，不從失異俗心，從之則滋害。

translations.literal: If they are allowed to carry tribute tea and given patents of appointment, in the event they falsely invoke imperial will to entice Qiang people and make reckless requests—refusal would lose the hearts of foreign peoples, and compliance would multiply harm.
translations.idiomatic: If we allow them to carry tribute tea and grant them patents of appointment, they may falsely invoke imperial authority to entice Qiang tribes and make reckless demands—refusal would alienate foreign peoples, and compliance would multiply the harm.

sentences.zh: 」奏上，罷賫茶，卒與誥命。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, the tribute tea was stopped, but in the end the patent was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, the tribute tea was denied, but in the end the patent was granted.

sentences.zh: 春又奏：「西番俗信佛教，故祖宗承前代舊，設立烏思藏諸司，及陜西洮、岷，四川松潘諸寺，令化導番人，許之朝貢。

translations.literal: Chun also memorialized: "Western tribes by custom believe in Buddhism; therefore the imperial ancestors, following former dynasties, established the various offices of U-Tsang and monasteries at Tao and Min in Shaanxi and Songpan in Sichuan, ordering them to guide and convert the tribal peoples and permitting them to come in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chun also memorialized: "The western tribes believe in Buddhism by custom; therefore our imperial ancestors, following earlier dynasties, established the various offices of U-Tsang and the monasteries at Tao and Min in Shaanxi and Songpan in Sichuan to guide and convert the tribal peoples and permit them to come in tribute.

sentences.zh: 貢期、人數皆有定制。

translations.literal: Tribute periods and numbers of envoys each had fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The periods and numbers of tribute missions were each fixed by regulation.

sentences.zh: 比緣諸番僻遠，莫辨真偽。

translations.literal: Recently, because the various tribes are remote and obscure, true and false cannot be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because the tribes are remote and obscure, true and false envoys can no longer be distinguished.

sentences.zh: 中國逃亡罪人，習其語言，竄身在內，又多創寺請額。

translations.literal: Fugitive criminals from China, having learned their languages, slipped in among them, and many also founded monasteries and requested imperial plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitive criminals from China, having learned tribal languages, slipped in among them, and many also founded monasteries and requested imperial plaques.

sentences.zh: 番貢日增，宴賞繁費，乞嚴其期限，酌定人數，每寺給勘合十道，緣邊兵備存勘合底簿，比對相同，方許起送。

translations.literal: Tribal tribute missions increase daily and banquets and rewards are extravagantly costly; I ask that deadlines be strictly enforced, numbers of envoys set appropriately, that each monastery be given ten tally-verifications, that border military officials keep the tally registers, and that embassies be permitted to depart only when the tallies match.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal tribute missions increase daily while banquets and rewards grow extravagantly costly; I ask that deadlines be strictly enforced, numbers of envoys set appropriately, that each monastery be issued ten tally-verifications, that border military officials keep the tally registers, and that missions be permitted to depart only when the tallies match.

sentences.zh: 並禁自後不得濫營寺宇。

translations.literal: And forbid henceforth the indiscriminate founding of monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: And forbid henceforth the indiscriminate founding of monasteries.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " The response approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 廣東布政使羅榮等入覲，各言鎮守內臣入貢之害。

translations.literal: Guangdong Administrative Commissioner Luo Rong and others came to audience and each spoke of the harm of resident eunuchs' tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong administrative commissioner Luo Rong and others came to audience and each spoke of the harm caused by resident eunuchs' tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 春列上累朝停革貢獻詔旨，且言四方水旱盜賊，軍民困苦狀，乞罷諸鎮守臣。

translations.literal: Chun listed edicts of successive reigns halting and abolishing tribute presentations, and also set forth conditions of flood, drought, and banditry in all directions and the distress of army and people, asking that all resident eunuch officials be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Chun listed edicts of successive reigns halting and abolishing tribute missions, described floods, droughts, and banditry across the realm and the distress of soldiers and civilians, and asked that all resident eunuch officials be abolished.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 春掌禮三年，慎守彜典。

translations.literal: Chun held the rites portfolio for three years and carefully guarded the canonical rites.
translations.idiomatic: Chun held the rites portfolio for three years and carefully upheld the canonical ritual code.

sentences.zh: 宗藩請封、請婚及文武大臣祭葬、贈謚，多所裁正。

translations.literal: On imperial clansmen's requests for enfeoffment and marriage, and civil and military ministers' funeral rites, posthumous honors, and posthumous titles, he corrected many.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial clansmen petitioned for enfeoffment or marriage, and when civil and military officials sought funeral rites, posthumous honors, and posthumous titles, he corrected many such requests.

sentences.zh: 遭憂，服闋起南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Having encountered bereavement, when mourning ended he was raised as Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After a bereavement, when his mourning period ended he was recalled as Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋以禮部尚書專典誥敕，掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward as Minister of Rites he was charged exclusively with drafting patent letters and edicts, and directed the affairs of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of Rites, charged exclusively with drafting edicts and patent letters, and directed the affairs of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚，文簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 劉氏世以科第顯。

translations.literal: The Liu clan through generations was prominent through the examination system.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu clan had been prominent for generations through the examination system.

sentences.zh: 春父規，御史。

translations.literal: Chun's father Gui was a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's father Gui served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 弟臺，雲南參政。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tai was administration vice commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tai served as administration vice commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 子彭年，巡撫貴州右副都御史。

translations.literal: His son Pengnian was vice censor-in-chief governing Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pengnian served as vice censor-in-chief and governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 彭年子起宗，遼東苑馬寺卿。

translations.literal: Pengnian's son Qizong was director of the Liaodong Stud Farm Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian's son Qizong served as director of the Liaodong Stud Farm Directorate.

sentences.zh: 起宗子世賞，廣東左布政使。

translations.literal: Qizong's son Shishang was left administrative commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Qizong's son Shishang served as left administrative commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 臺子鶴年，雲南布政使，以清譽聞。

translations.literal: Tai's son Henian was administrative commissioner of Yunnan, known for a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's son Henian served as administrative commissioner of Yunnan and was known for his reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 鶴年孫世曾，巡撫雲南右副都御史，有征緬功。

translations.literal: Henian's grandson Shizeng was vice censor-in-chief governing Yunnan, with merit in the Burma campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Henian's grandson Shizeng served as vice censor-in-chief and governor of Yunnan, with merit in the campaign against Burma.

sentences.zh: 皆由進士。

translations.literal: All entered through the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: All had entered office through the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 吳儼，字克溫，宜興人。

translations.literal: Wu Yan, styled Kewen, was a man of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan, styled Kewen, was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the twenty-third year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-third year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修，歷侍講學士，掌南京翰林院。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, appointed compiler, served successively as expositor and reader, and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, appointed compiler, served successively as expositor and reader, and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 正德初，召修《孝宗實錄》，直講筵。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengde, summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong and served in the lecturing presence.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign he was summoned to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong and served in the imperial lecturing presence.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾竊柄，聞儼家多資，遣人啖以美官。

translations.literal: Liu Jin usurped power; hearing Yan's family had much wealth, he sent men to lure with a fine office.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin usurped power, hearing that Yan's family was wealthy, he sent men to lure him with a fine office.

sentences.zh: 儼峻拒之，瑾怒。

translations.literal: Yan sternly refused; Jin grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sternly refused, and Jin grew angry.

sentences.zh: 會大計群吏，中旨罷儼官。

translations.literal: At the grand evaluation of officials, an edict from the inner court removed Yan from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand evaluation of officials, an edict from the inner court removed Yan from office.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復職歷禮部左、右侍郎，拜南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, restored to office, served successively as left and right vice minister of rites, and was appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Yan was restored to office, served successively as left and right vice minister of rites, and was appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十二年，武宗北巡，儼抗疏切諫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when Emperor Wuzong toured the north, Yan submitted a forceful memorial strongly remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when Emperor Wuzong toured the north, Yan submitted a forceful memorial strongly remonstrating.

sentences.zh: 明年復偕諸大臣上疏曰：「臣等初聞駕幸昌平，曾具疏極論，不蒙采納。

translations.literal: The next year he again joined the senior ministers in a memorial, saying: "We first heard the imperial carriage would visit Changping and submitted a memorial arguing at length, but it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again joined the senior ministers in a memorial, saying: "We first heard that Your Majesty would visit Changping and submitted a memorial arguing at length, but it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 既聞出居庸，幸宣、大，宰輔不及知，群臣不及從，三軍之士不及衛，京師內外人心動搖。

translations.literal: Now we hear of departure through Juyong, proceeding to Xuan and Da; the chief ministers had no advance knowledge, the assembled officials could not follow, the soldiers of the three armies could not guard, and hearts within and outside the capital are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear that Your Majesty has passed through Juyong and proceeded to Xuanfu and Datong; the chief ministers had no advance knowledge, the assembled officials could not follow, the soldiers of the three armies could not guard, and hearts within and outside the capital are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 徐、淮以南，荒饉千里，去冬雨雪為災，民無衣食，安保其不為盜。

translations.literal: South of Xu and Huai, famine stretches a thousand li; last winter snow and rain brought disaster, the people lack food and clothing—how can one ensure they will not become bandits?
translations.idiomatic: South of Xu and Huai, famine stretches a thousand li; last winter snow and rain brought disaster, and the people lack food and clothing—how can one ensure they will not turn to banditry?

sentences.zh: 所禦之寇尚遠隔陰山，而不虞之禍或猝起於肘腋，臣所大懼也。

translations.literal: The enemy we guard against is still far beyond the Yin Mountains, yet unanticipated calamity may suddenly arise at our very side—this is what we greatly fear.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy we guard against is still far beyond the Yin Mountains, yet unanticipated calamity may suddenly arise at our very side—this is what we greatly fear.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No response.
translations.idiomatic: " No response was given.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚文肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 顧清，字士廉，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Gu Qing, styled Shilian, was a man of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Qing, styled Shilian, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，成進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the metropolitan examination, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he passed the metropolitan examination, was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 與同年生毛澄、羅欽順、汪俊相砥以名節。

translations.literal: With his examination cohort Mao Cheng, Luo Qinshun, and Wang Jun he sharpened one another in reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: With his examination cohort Mao Cheng, Luo Qinshun, and Wang Jun he sharpened one another in reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 進侍讀。

translations.literal: Promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 正德初，劉瑾竊柄，清邑子張文冕為謀主，附者立尊顯。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengde, Liu Jin usurped power; Qing's fellow townsman Zhang Wenmian served as chief strategist, and those who attached themselves were swiftly elevated.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhengde reign, when Liu Jin usurped power, Qing's fellow townsman Zhang Wenmian served as chief strategist; those who attached themselves to him were swiftly elevated.

sentences.zh: 清絕不與通，瑾銜之。

translations.literal: Qing utterly refused dealings with them; Jin bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Qing utterly refused to have dealings with them, and Jin bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 四年摘《會典》小誤，挫諸翰林，清降編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, seizing on a minor error in the Collected Statutes, he humbled the Hanlin academicians; Qing was demoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, seizing on a minor error in the Collected Statutes, Jin humbled the Hanlin academicians; Qing was demoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 又以諸翰林未諳政事，調外任及兩京部屬，清得南京兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Further, on grounds that Hanlin scholars were unfamiliar with state affairs, they were transferred to outside posts and subordinate positions in both capitals; Qing received the post of secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: On further grounds that Hanlin scholars were unfamiliar with state affairs, they were transferred to outside posts and subordinate positions in both capitals; Qing was assigned as secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 會父憂，不赴。

translations.literal: Just then his father died; he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Just then his father died, and he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，還侍讀，擢侍讀學士掌院事。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, restored as reader, promoted to reading bachelor directing academy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Qing returned as reader, was promoted to reading bachelor, and directed academy affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋遷少詹事，充經筵日講官，進禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to junior tutor of the heir apparent, served as daily lecturer at the classics colloquium, and was promoted to right vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to junior tutor of the heir apparent, served as daily lecturer at the classics colloquium, and was promoted to right vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時澄已為尚書，清協恭守職，前後請建儲宮，罷巡幸，疏凡十數上。

translations.literal: By then Cheng was already minister; Qing worked collaboratively and diligently in office, and before and after submitted more than a dozen memorials requesting establishment of the crown prince and cessation of imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: By then Mao Cheng was already minister; Qing worked collaboratively and diligently in office, and submitted more than a dozen memorials requesting the establishment of a crown prince and the cessation of imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，為御史李獻所劾，罷歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, impeached by censor Li Xian, dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was impeached by censor Li Xian and dismissed to return home.

sentences.zh: 清學端行謹，恬於進取。

translations.literal: Qing's learning was upright, his conduct careful, and he was indifferent to advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's learning was upright, his conduct careful, and he was indifferent to advancement.

sentences.zh: 家居，薦者相繼，悉報寢。

translations.literal: While at home, recommenders came one after another; all nominations were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: While at home, recommenders came one after another, but all nominations were shelved.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，詔舉老成堪用內閣者，廷推及清，乃以為南京禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing, an edict called for recommendations of seasoned men fit for the grand secretariat; the court nomination reached Qing, and he was appointed right vice minister of rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing, an edict called for recommendations of seasoned men fit for the grand secretariat; the court nomination reached Qing, and he was appointed right vice minister of rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 上言：「錦衣職侍衛，祖宗朝非機密不遣。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The duty of the Embroidered Uniform Guard is attendance and protection; in the reigns of the ancestral emperors they were not dispatched except on confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "The duty of the Embroidered Uniform Guard is attendance and protection; in the reigns of our ancestral emperors they were not dispatched except on confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 正德間，營差四出，海內騷然，陛下所親見。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde period, commissions were sent out in all directions and the realm was thrown into turmoil—Your Majesty saw this with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde period, commissions were sent out in all directions and the realm was thrown into turmoil—Your Majesty saw this with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 近乃遣千戶勘揚州高瀹爭私財事，囚其女婦，憯毒備加。

translations.literal: Recently a chiliarch was sent to investigate a private property dispute involving Gao Yue of Yangzhou; his daughters and daughters-in-law were imprisoned and subjected to every cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a chiliarch was sent to investigate a private property dispute involving Gao Yue of Yangzhou; his daughters and daughters-in-law were imprisoned and subjected to every cruelty.

sentences.zh: 請自今悉付所司，停旗校無遣。

translations.literal: I ask that henceforth all such matters be entrusted to the proper offices and that banner officers and guard deputies be stopped from dispatch entirely.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that henceforth all such matters be entrusted to the proper offices and that banner officers and guard deputies cease to be dispatched entirely.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 屢疏引疾，詔進尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Repeatedly memorialized citing illness; an edict promoted him to minister and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized citing illness; an edict promoted him to minister and granted him retirement.

sentences.zh: 時方進表入都，道卒。

translations.literal: Just then, as he was submitting a memorial on the road to the capital, he died en route.
translations.idiomatic: Just then, as he was submitting a memorial on the road to the capital, he died en route.

sentences.zh: 謚文僖。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 劉瑞，字德符，內江人。

translations.literal: Liu Rui, styled Defu, was a man of Neijiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rui, styled Defu, was a native of Neijiang.

sentences.zh: 父時斅，官山東僉事，以廉惠稱。

translations.literal: His father Shixiao served as surveillance vice commissioner of Shandong and was known for integrity and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shixiao served as surveillance vice commissioner of Shandong and was known for integrity and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 瑞舉弘治九年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Rui passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Hongzhi, was selected as Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Rui passed the metropolitan examination in the ninth year of Hongzhi, was selected as Hanlin Bachelor, and appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 好學潔修，遇事輒有論建。

translations.literal: He loved learning and cultivated purity in conduct; whenever events arose he had proposals to offer.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and cultivated purity in conduct; whenever events arose he had proposals to offer.

sentences.zh: 清寧宮災，請罷醮壇。

translations.literal: When the Qingning Palace burned, he requested that Daoist altars of supplication be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qingning Palace burned, he requested that Daoist altars of supplication be abolished.

sentences.zh: 時召內閣講官延訪治道，又言：「故閹李廣門下內臣，宜悉治罪。

translations.literal: At the time the throne summoned grand secretariat lecturers to consult on the Way of governance, and he also said: "The palace eunuchs who were under the disgraced eunuch Li Guang should all be punished.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the throne summoned grand secretariat lecturers to consult on the Way of governance, and he also said: "The palace eunuchs who were under the disgraced eunuch Li Guang should all be punished.

sentences.zh: 前太監汪直，先帝罪人，今來覬用，當斥遠之。

translations.literal: The former superintendent Wang Zhi was a criminal of the late emperor; now that he has come seeking employment again, he should be repudiated and kept afar.
translations.idiomatic: The former superintendent Wang Zhi was a criminal of the late emperor; now that he has come seeking employment again, he should be repudiated and kept at a distance.

sentences.zh: 副使楊茂元、郎中王雲鳳以直言獲罪，宜召復其官。

translations.literal: Vice commissioner Yang Maoyuan and director Wang Yunfeng were punished for forthright speech; they should be recalled and their offices restored.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Yang Maoyuan and director Wang Yunfeng were punished for forthright speech; they should be recalled and their offices restored.

sentences.zh: 京師之萬春宮，興濟真武廟、壽寧侯第，在外之興、岐、衡、雍、汝、涇諸府，土木繁興，宜悉罷不急者。

translations.literal: In the capital—the Wanchun Palace, the Xingji Zhenwu Temple, and the mansion of the Marquis of Shouning; in the provinces—the princely establishments at Xing, Qi, Heng, Yong, Ru, and Jing—construction projects flourish everywhere; all non-urgent works should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital—the Wanchun Palace, the Xingji Zhenwu Temple, and the mansion of the Marquis of Shouning; in the provinces—the princely establishments at Xing, Qi, Heng, Yong, Ru, and Jing—construction projects flourish everywhere; all non-urgent works should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 都勻之捷，鄧廷瓚冒其功。

translations.literal: At the victory at Duyun, Deng Tingzan usurped the credit.
translations.idiomatic: At the victory at Duyun, Deng Tingzan usurped the credit.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭之征，王越啟其釁。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Helan, Wang Yue provoked the conflict.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign at Helan, Wang Yue provoked the conflict.

sentences.zh: 請追正欺罔之罪。

translations.literal: I ask that the crime of deception be investigated and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the crime of deception be investigated and corrected.

sentences.zh: 」報聞。

translations.literal: " Acknowledgment returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 闕里廟成，遣大學士李東陽祭告。

translations.literal: When the Confucius temple at Qufu was completed, Grand Secretary Li Dongyang was dispatched to offer sacrifice and announcement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Confucius temple at Qufu was completed, Grand Secretary Li Dongyang was dispatched to offer sacrifice and announcement.

sentences.zh: 瑞請更定先師封謚，不果行。

translations.literal: Rui requested that the enfeoffment title and posthumous title of the Sage be revised; this was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Rui requested that the enfeoffment title and posthumous title of the Sage be revised, but this was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾用事，瑞即謝病。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin wielded power, Rui immediately pleaded illness and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin wielded power, Rui immediately pleaded illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 貧不能還鄉，依從母子李充嗣於澧州。

translations.literal: Too poor to return home, he relied on his maternal cousin Li Chongsi at Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to return home, he relied on his maternal cousin Li Chongsi at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 瑾榜瑞為奸黨，又以前薦雍泰除其名，罰米輸塞上。

translations.literal: Jin listed Rui among the faction of villains, and because he had previously recommended Yong Tai, struck his name from the rolls and fined him grain to be delivered to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Jin listed Rui among the faction of villains, and because he had previously recommended Yong Tai, struck his name from the rolls and fined him grain to be delivered to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 坐是益困，授徒自給。

translations.literal: For this he grew ever poorer and supported himself by teaching pupils.
translations.idiomatic: For this he grew ever poorer and supported himself by teaching pupils.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，以副使督浙江學校，召為南京太僕少卿。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, served as education intendant of Zhejiang, and was summoned as vice director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he served as education intendant of Zhejiang and was summoned as vice director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，由南太常卿就遷禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, from vice director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was directly promoted to right vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing, from vice director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was directly promoted to right vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 因災變偕同官條上六事，且言齋醮無益且妨政，織造多費且病民。

translations.literal: In response to natural calamities he joined his colleagues in submitting six items in sequence, and also stated that fasting and Daoist rites were of no benefit and obstructed governance, while excessive weaving and manufacturing wasted resources and harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: In response to natural calamities he joined his colleagues in submitting six items in sequence, and also stated that fasting and Daoist rites were of no benefit and obstructed governance, while excessive weaving and manufacturing wasted resources and harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 帝多納用之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted and enacted much of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted and enacted much of this.

sentences.zh: 大禮議起，瑞偕九卿合疏。

translations.literal: When the Grand Rites controversy arose, Rui joined the nine chief ministers in a joint memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Rites controversy arose, Rui joined the nine chief ministers in a joint memorial.

sentences.zh: 極言大宗、小宗之義，凡數千言。

translations.literal: He expounded at length on the principles of the major and minor lineages, in several thousand words altogether.
translations.idiomatic: He expounded at length on the principles of the major and minor lineages, in several thousand words altogether.

sentences.zh: 四年卒官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously honored as minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as minister.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，謚文肅。

translations.literal: At the start of Longqing, posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longqing reign he was given the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：周洪謨等以詞臣歷卿貳。

translations.literal: The chronicler commends: Zhou Hongmo and the others rose from literary officials to vice-ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler commends: Zhou Hongmo and the others rose from literary officials to vice-ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 或職事拳拳，或侃侃建白，進講以啟沃為心，守官以獻替自效。

translations.literal: Some were scrupulous in their duties, some spoke forthrightly in memorials; in lecturing they took nourishing the ruler as their aim, in holding office they took offering counsel and replacement as their service.
translations.idiomatic: Some were scrupulous in their duties, some spoke forthrightly in memorials; in lecturing they took nourishing the ruler as their aim, in holding office they took offering counsel and replacement as their service.

sentences.zh: 於文學侍從之選，均無愧諸。

translations.literal: Among those chosen for literary service at court, none fell short of the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Among those chosen for literary service at court, none fell short of the standard.
